table_description: This table stores a master list of programs available for patients to enroll in for different features, such as Chronic Care Management (CCM) and Transition Care Management (TCM).

columns.name: id
columns.description: The column stores an id of the acoprograms. This is an auto incremental primary key of This column .

columns.name: program
columns.description: This column saves the program name created by the user. The type of program created is identified by the programtype column

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 indicating this program is deleted. This is soft delete. 0 - Not Deleted and 1 -Deleted.

columns.name: localflag
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 indicating a local flag. By default, it is saved as 0.

columns.name: ProgramType
columns.description: This column stores the program type for which the program is created by the user. This refers to the id column from the programtype table.

columns.name: programterm
columns.description: This column stores the duration of the program created. Values that can be stored in varchar (e.g., 2 months, 1 year).

columns.name: displayIndex
columns.description: This column saves the incremental value called as display index. This value denotes the order in which the records are shown on the front end.

table_description: This table stores information about the player participated in the events.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each attendance record. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: Activityid
columns.description: identifier for the activity that the user attended. This is a foreign key that refers to the id column in the activities table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: identifier for the user who attended the activity. This is a foreign key that refers to the id column in the user table. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: status
columns.description: The status of the user's attendance, such as Active(Full-Go) or Limited/Restricted. Example: Active(Full-Go), Limited/Restricted, Probable, Questionable, Doubtful.

columns.name: attended
columns.description: A binary flag indicating whether the user attended the activity (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: A binary flag indicating whether the attendance record has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: injurylink
columns.description: This column stores ids for injury selected. The column has been declared as VARCHAR because this column may store multiple ids for diagnosis separated by ',' (i.e., 250909,252643).

columns.name: OtherReason
columns.description: A brief description of any other reason for the user's attendance status, if applicable. Example: family emergency, car trouble).

table_description: This table stores information about activities and events in a calendar, including their start and end times, recurrence patterns, and related metadata.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key of This column  and is an auto incremented value.

columns.name: Title
columns.description: The title or name of the activity or event. Example: team meeting, birthday party.

columns.name: StartDate
columns.description: The date when the activity or event starts. Example: 2022-01-01.

columns.name: StartTime
columns.description: The time when the activity or event starts. Example: 14:00:00.

columns.name: EndDate
columns.description: The date when the activity or event ends. Example: 2022-01-01.

columns.name: EndTime
columns.description: The time when the activity or event ends. Example: 16:00:00.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: A flag indicating if the activity or event has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: AllDay
columns.description: A flag indicating if the activity or event is an all-day event (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: CreatedDate
columns.description: The time stamp when the activity or event was created. Example: 2022-01-01 12:00:00.

columns.name: ModifiedDate
columns.description: The time stamp when the activity or event was last modified. Example: 2022-01-02 12:00:00.

columns.name: RecFlag
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

columns.name: RecStartDate
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

columns.name: RecEndInfo
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

columns.name: RecPattern
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

columns.name: RecPatternEvery
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

columns.name: createuserid
columns.description: This column  stores the user id of the user who created the event. This refers to the UID column of the user table.

columns.name: moduserid
columns.description: The unique identifier of the user who last modified the activity or event. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: facilityid
columns.description: This column  stores the facility id of the event where it is created. This refers to the id column of the edi_facilities table.

table_description: This table stores detailed information about various activities, including their type, location, season, status, equipment, surface, and other related attributes.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key of This column . It is an autoincremented value.

columns.name: Activityid
columns.description: This stores the activity id of the activity. This refers to the id column of the activitycalendar table.

columns.name: Type
columns.description: The type of activity. Example: Running, Swimming, Cycling.

columns.name: Location
columns.description: This column  stores the location code of the activity. This refers to the code column of the activitydetailinfo table.

columns.name: SeasonType
columns.description: The type of season during which the activity occurs. Example: Winter, Summer, Spring, Autumn.

columns.name: Status
columns.description: This column  stores the status of the activity. Example: Complete, Reschedule.

columns.name: Equipment
columns.description: This column  stores the equipment id for the activity. This refers to code column of the athletics_activity_equipment table.

columns.name: Surface
columns.description: The surface on which the activity takes place. Example: Grass, Concrete, Sand.

columns.name: SurfaceType
columns.description: This column  stores the surface type id selected  for the activity. This refers to code column of athletics_activity_surfaceType table.

columns.name: ConditionType
columns.description: The type of condition during the activity. Example: Sunny, Rainy, Windy.

columns.name: Temperature
columns.description: This column  stores the temperature of the activity in degree fahrenheit.

columns.name: Humidity
columns.description: This column  stores the humidity of the activity in percentage.

columns.name: Season
columns.description: This column  stores the season code of the activity. This refers to code column of the activitydetailinfo table.

columns.name: GameLocation
columns.description: This column  stores the code of home location of the activity. This refers to code column of the activitydetailinfo table.

columns.name: Opponent
columns.description: The opponent team or player for competitive activities. Example: Team X, Player Y, Club Z.

columns.name: StadiumType
columns.description: The type of stadium where the activity takes place. Example: Indoor, Outdoor, Dome.

columns.name: GameWeek
columns.description: The week of the game for team sports. Example: Week 1, Week 2, Week 3.

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: This column stores the notes of the activity.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column store values 0/1 to indicate whether the item has been marked deleted or not. 0 - item is not marked deleted, 1 - item is marked deleted.

columns.name: setCurrentStatus
columns.description: A flag indicating if the current status should be set. Example: 0 (do not set), 1 (set).

columns.name: SportId
columns.description: This column is not in use anymore

table_description: This table stores additional addresses for patients, including details such as address lines, city, Zip Code, state, country, and the type of address.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each additional address entry. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: Foreign key referring to the patient's unique identifier in the `patient` table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: AddressLine1
columns.description: First line of the additional address. Example: "123 Main St", "456 Elm St".

columns.name: AddressLine2
columns.description: Second line of the additional address, typically used for apartment or suite numbers. Example: "Apt 4B", "Suite 300".

columns.name: city
columns.description: City where the additional address is located. Example: "New York", "Los Angeles".

columns.name: zip
columns.description: Zip code of the additional address. Example: "10001", "90001".

columns.name: state
columns.description: State where the additional address is located. Example: "New York", "California".

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country where the additional address is located. Example: "United States", "Canada".

columns.name: isPrimary
columns.description: This field stores 0 and from patientdemographics it can not be change to 1

columns.name: typeofaddress
columns.description: Type of the additional address, such as "home", "work", or "billing". Example: "home", "work".

table_description: This table stores additional notes related to patients, including information about the user who created the note, the date and time of the note, and any associated subject data.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each additional note. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: identifier for the patient associated with the note. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: LoggedInUID
columns.description: identifier for the user who was logged in when the note was created. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date when the note was created. Example: 2021-09-15, 2021-09-16, 2021-09-17.

columns.name: time
columns.description: The time when the note was created. Example: 14:30:00, 15:45:00, 16:00:00.

columns.name: Message
columns.description: The text content of the additional note. Example: patient reported mild headache, patient's blood pressure is stable, patient is recovering well from surgery.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: Indicates whether the note has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: moduleName
columns.description: Name of the module where the note was created. Example: PatientHistory, lLabResults, Prescriptions.

columns.name: createdOn
columns.description: The date and time when the note was created. Example: 2021-09-15 14:30:00, 2021-09-16 15:45:00, 2021-09-17 16:00:00.

columns.name: createdBy
columns.description: identifier for the user who created the note. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003. Foreign key relation: users (UID).

columns.name: subjectData
columns.description: Additional subject-related data for the note. Example: Migraine, Hypertension, Post-surgery.

table_description: This table stores address information for patients in the system.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each address entry. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: patientId
columns.description: Identifier for the patient associated with the address. This is a foreign key that refers to the `patients` table's `pid` column. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: AddressStatus
columns.description: Indicates whether the address is current address (1) or previous Address (0). Example: 1, 0.

columns.name: Address_type_id
columns.description: Indicates diffrent addresstype from addresstypetable example 2 business, 3 Campus,4 International

columns.name: addressline1
columns.description: First line of the address. Example: "123 Main St."

columns.name: addressline2
columns.description: Second line of the address (optional). Example: "Apt 4B."

columns.name: Effectivedatefrom
columns.description: It shows the date on which patient is moved into this address

columns.name: Effectivedateto
columns.description: It shows the date on which patient is moved out from this address

columns.name: city
columns.description: City where the address is located. Example: "New York."

columns.name: County
columns.description: County where the address is located. Example: "Kings County."

columns.name: state
columns.description: State where the address is located. Example: "NY."

columns.name: zip
columns.description: Zip code of the address. Example: "10001."

columns.name: Country
columns.description: Country where the address is located. Example: "US."

columns.name: countycode
columns.description: Code for the county where the address is located. Example: "36047."

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: Indicates whether the address entry has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 1, 0.

table_description: This table stores information about different types of addresses.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits and is automatically incremented for each new record. Example values: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Address_type_id
columns.description: This column stores a unique identifier for each address type. It is an integer with a maximum length of 2 digits. Example values: 01, 02, 03, etc.

columns.name: Address_type_Desc
columns.description: This column stores a description of the address type. It is a variable character string with a maximum length of 50 characters. Example values: "Home Address", "Work Address", "Billing Address", etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column indicates whether the record has been deleted or not. It is a tiny integer with a length of 1 digit and has a default value of '0'. A value of '0' means the record is not deleted, while a value of '1' means the record is deleted. Example values: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores information about adjustment postings related to inventory, line items, and amounts.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each adjustment posting record. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: Adjustmentid
columns.description: This column  is used to store the Adjustment ID.

columns.name: Invid
columns.description: This column is used to store the Invoice ID.

columns.name: LineItemid
columns.description: This column is used to store the Line Item ID.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The amount of the adjustment posting, stored as a decimal value with 9 digits and 2 decimal places. Example: 150.25, 300.50, 450.75.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the record has been deleted or not. A value of 0 means not deleted, and a value of 1 means deleted. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: AddedBy
columns.description: identifier for the user who added the adjustment posting record. This is a foreign key that refers to the id column in the user table. Example: 10, 11, 12.

columns.name: AddedTime
columns.description: The date and time when the adjustment posting record was added, stored as a date time value. Example: 2021-09-01 12:34:56, 2021-09-02 14:30:00.

columns.name: UpdatedBy
columns.description: identifier for the user who last updated the adjustment posting record. This is a foreign key that refers to the id` column in the user table. Example: 10, 11, 12.

columns.name: UpdatedTime
columns.description: The date and time when the adjustment posting record was last updated, stored as a date time value. Example: 2021-09-01 12:34:56, 2021-09-02 14:30:00.

columns.name: closingid
columns.description: This column is used to store the Closing ID.

columns.name: discountType
columns.description: A tiny integer value representing the type of discount applied to the adjustment posting. Example: 0, 1, 2.

table_description: This tables stores a list of Drug Administration sites created by end users.

columns.description: This is an auto-incremented primary key in this column.

columns.name: SiteDesc
columns.description: This column stores free text description of the site entered by the end user while creating the Drug Administration site.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the drug administration site is active or not.

columns.name: modifiedBy
columns.description: This column stores an id of a user who modified the existing Drug Administration site. This column refers to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: modifiedDateTime
columns.description: This column stores date and time when the Drug Administration site was modified by the end user. Date and time is stored in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.sss format.

columns.name: createdBy
columns.description: This column stores an id of a user who created the Drug Administration site. This column refers to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: This column stores date and time when the Drug Administration site was created by the end user. Date and time is stored in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.sss format.

columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented for each new record. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Code
columns.description: This column stores a unique code associated with each advance directive. It is a variable character field with a maximum length of 25 characters. Example: AD001, AD002, AD003, etc.

columns.name: Name
columns.description: This column stores the name or description of the advance directive. It is a variable character field with a maximum length of 255 characters. Example: Do Not Resuscitate, Living Will, Healthcare Power of Attorney, etc.

table_description: This table stores information related to Antenatal Fetal Protein (AFP) tests, which are used to screen for certain birth defects during pregnancy.

columns.name: reportid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each AFP report. It is a primary key for the labdata table.

columns.name: insulinDependent
columns.description: This column indicates whether the patient is insulin-dependent (1) or not (0).

columns.name: GAweeks
columns.description: Gestational age in weeks (e.g., 12, 24, 36).

columns.name: GADays
columns.description: Gestational age in days (e.g., 1, 15, 30).

columns.name: GAdecimal
columns.description: Gestational age in decimal format (e.g., 12.5, 24.3, 36.7).

columns.name: GAdate
columns.description: Date of gestational age calculation (e.g., 2021-01-01, 2021-06-15, 2021-12-31).

columns.name: GAbyLMP
columns.description: Indicates whether the gestational age is calculated by the last menstrual period (LMP) (1) or not (0).

columns.name: lmpDate
columns.description: Date of the last menstrual period (e.g., 2021-01-01, 2021-06-15, 2021-12-31).

columns.name: GAbyUltrasound
columns.description: Indicates whether the gestational age is calculated by ultrasound (1) or not (0).

columns.name: GAbyDeliveryDate
columns.description: Indicates whether the gestational age is calculated by the delivery date (1) or not (0).

columns.name: pregnancyType
columns.description: Type of pregnancy (e.g., singleton, twins, triplets).

columns.name: routineScreening
columns.description: Indicates whether the AFP test is part of routine screening (1) or not (0).

columns.name: neuralTubeDefects
columns.description: Indicates whether the AFP test is for neural tube defects (1) or not (0).

columns.name: advancedMaternalAge
columns.description: Indicates whether the mother has advanced maternal age (1) or not (0).

columns.name: downSyndrome
columns.description: Indicates whether the AFP test is for down syndrome (1) or not (0).

columns.name: cysticFibriosis
columns.description: Indicates whether the AFP test is for cystic fibrosis (1) or not (0).

columns.name: otherIndications
columns.description: Indicates whether there are other indications for the AFP test (1) or not (0).

columns.name: handWrittenInfo
columns.description: Indicates whether the AFP report contains handwritten information (1) or not (0).

columns.name: reasonElevated
columns.description: Indicates whether there is a reason for elevated AFP levels (1) or not (0).

columns.name: earlyGA
columns.description: Indicates whether the gestational age is considered early (1) or not (0).

columns.name: Hemolyzed
columns.description: Indicates whether the blood sample is hemolyzed (1) or not (0).

columns.name: weight
columns.description: Patient's weight (e.g., 60, 70, 80).

columns.name: race
columns.description: Patient's race (e.g., Caucasian, African American, Asian).

table_description: This table stores information about aftercare status codes, including their unique code, status, color, and whether they are billable or not.

columns.name: codeid
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which is an integer that uniquely identifies each aftercare status code. It is auto-incremented, meaning that it will automatically increase in value as new records are added. Example values: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: code
columns.description: This column stores abbreviated codes for different statuses used in the AfterCare module.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This is a unique varchar column that stores the description of the aftercare status. Example values: Completed, In Progress, Cancelled, etc.

columns.name: color
columns.description: This is a unique varchar column that stores the color associated with each aftercare status for display purposes. Example values: red, blue, green, etc.

columns.name: NonBillable
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the status is Billable or Non Billable.

table_description: This table stores aftercare history status data for the encounter.

columns.name: statusHistoryid
columns.description: This column is an auto incremented primary key in this column. Unique status history id is assigned to each record when they are created using the user interface.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores the id of an encounter for which aftercare status history related to the patient's visit is documented. This column refers to the column encounterid from the enc table.

columns.name: code
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history status code. This column refers to the column code from the aftercare status codes table.

columns.name: date
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history status created date.

columns.name: time
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history status created time.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of the user who has created the aftercare status history. It refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: substatuscode
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history sub status code. This column refers to the column code from the aftercare sub status codes table.

table_description: This table stores information about aftercare substatus codes, including their unique code, substatus, and a delete flag.

columns.name: codeid
columns.description: This column is an auto-incremented primary key in this column. Unique code id is assigned to each record when they are created using the User Interface.

columns.name: code
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history sub status code.

columns.name: substatus
columns.description: This column stores the aftercare history sub status.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the record has been marked as deleted or not.

table_description: This table stores the CDSS Alerts calculated for patients.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is an auto incremented primary key for this column.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores an id of the patient who is eligible for the CDSS enabled alert from the Measureid column. This column refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: Measureid
columns.description: This column stores id of the measure/alert for which that particular patient is eligible. This column refers to the column Measureid from the measureconfiguration table.

columns.name: MeasureName
columns.description: This column stores the name of the measure from the Measureid column. This column refers to the MeasureName column from the measuredefinitions table.

columns.name: Itemid
columns.description: This column stores an id of the item selected which is used to render the patient's compliant with the alert. This column refers to the column itemid from the items table.

columns.name: Frequency
columns.description: This column stores the frequency of the alert. This column refers to the column paraValue from the measureparaconfig table.

columns.name: LastDone
columns.description: This column stores the date when the test was last ordered for the alert in Measureid column. The format used is MM/DD/YYYY.

columns.name: DueDate
columns.description: This column stores the date when the alert is next due for the patient. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: Value
columns.description: This column stores the results of the ordered test.

columns.name: controlstatus
columns.description: This column stores the current status of the alert for the patient: 1 - Compliant, 2 - Pending Results, 3 - Noncompliant or Suppressed, 4 - Excluded.

columns.name: RegistryAlert
columns.description: This column stores flags 0 or 1.

columns.name: labReceived
columns.description: This column stores flags 0 or 1.

columns.name: mdate
columns.description: This column stores the current time stamp when the CDSS alert is calculated for the eligible patient. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

columns.name: isExternalAlert
columns.description: This column stores flag 0 or 1. 1 - alert was received from an external source through healow insights, and 0 -  alert was not received from an external source.

columns.name: isMergedToCdssAlert
columns.description: This column stores flags 0 or 1. 1 - alert is an external alert that was merged with a CDSS alert, and 0 - otherwise.

table_description: This table is used to handle concurrency while CDSS alerts are being calculated for a patient.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a patient who qualifies for the CDSS alerts. This column refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: isInsertInProgress
columns.description: This column stores a flag 0 or 1. 1- while CDSS alerts are being calculated, and 0 - when CDSS alerts calculation finished.

columns.name: lockTakenAt
columns.description: This column stores the current time stamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format.

table_description: This table stores the suppression status of CDSS Alerts for patients.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is an auto incremented primary key for this column.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores an id of the patient for whom alerts are suppressed. This column refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: Measureid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the measure/alert which is suppressed for a patient. This column refers to the column Measureid from the measureconfiguration table.

columns.name: DueDate
columns.description: This column stores the date until which the alert in the Measureid column is suppressed. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.

columns.name: NeverRemind
columns.description: This column stores flag 0 or 1. 1 - permanent suppression of alerts, and 0 - temporary  suppression of alerts.

columns.name: Reason
columns.description: This column stores the free text reason documented by the end user as to why the alert in Measureid column is suppressed.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores one of the below pre- defined values as status. 1P, 2P, 3P and ERRONEOUS. These values are mapped with the values in statusLabel column respectively. 1P - MEDICAL REASON, 2P - PATIENT REASON, 3P - SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS - ERRONEOUSDIAGNOSES.

columns.name: statusLabel
columns.description: This column stores one of the below pre-defined values as status label. MEDICAL REASON, PATIENT REASON, SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS DIAGNOSES. These values are mapped with the values in status column respectively. 1P - MEDICAL REASON, 2P - PATIENT REASON, 3P - SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS - ERRONEOUSDIAGNOSES.

columns.name: reset
columns.description: This column stores flags 0 or 1. 1 - if the suppression has been reset, and 0 - if the suppression has not been reset.

table_description: This table stores additional information related to the suppression status of CDSS Alerts for patients.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is an auto incremented primary key for this column.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores an id of the patient for whom alerts are suppressed. This column refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: Measureid
columns.description: This column stores id of the measure/alert which is suppressed for a patient. This column refers to the column Measureid from the measureconfiguration table.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores 0 if the alert is suppressed from Patient Hub or the encounter id if it is suppressed from the Progress Note.

columns.name: TrUserid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the user who suppressed the alert for a patient. This column refers to the column UID from the user table.

columns.name: NeverRemind
columns.description: This column stores flag 0 or 1. 1 - permanent suppression of alerts, and 0 - temporary suppression of alerts.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores one of the below pre-defined values as status. 1P, 2P, 3P and ERRONEOUS. These values are mapped with the values in the statusLabel column respectively. 1P - MEDICAL REASON, 2P - PATIENT REASON, 3P - SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS - ERRONEOUSDIAGNOSES.

columns.name: statusLabel
columns.description: This column stores one of the below pre-defined values as status label. MEDICAL REASON, PATIENT REASON, SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS DIAGNOSES. These values are mapped with the values in the status column respectively. 1P - MEDICAL REASON, 2P - PATIENT REASON, 3P - SYSTEM REASON & ERRONEOUS - ERRONEOUSDIAGNOSES.

columns.name: reset
columns.description: This column stores flags 0 or 1.

columns.name: modifiedtime
columns.description: This column stores a time stamp when the alert was suppressed. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

table_description: This table stores information about alerts that have been imported into the Progress Notes, including their type, status, and related encounter details.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is an auto incremented primary key.

columns.name: AlertType
columns.description: This column stores the type of an alert. Possible values are CDSS, Generic, patient specific, Rx specific, Dx specific, or multisatisfied.

columns.name: Alertid
columns.description: This column stores an id of the alert from the AlertType column.

columns.name: Encounterid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the encounter to which alert is imported. This column refers to the encounterid from the enc table.

columns.name: AlertName
columns.description: This column stores the name of the alert merged in the Progress Notes.

columns.name: DueDate
columns.description: This column indicates the alert's due date at the time it was imported to the Progress Notes. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:000. In case if there is no due date, NULL is stored.

columns.name: Status
columns.description: This column indicates the status of the alert. Possible values are Complaint, Suppressed,  Excluded, Non-Complaint, or pending results.

columns.name: LastDoneDate
columns.description: This column stores the date on which the test was ordered for a particular patient. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:000. In case if there is no last done date, NULL is stored.

columns.name: ActionTaken
columns.description: This column indicates if the auto imported alert was removed or manually imported. '-' for manually imported and 'removed auto imported' for auto imported removal.

columns.name: ImportedDate
columns.description: This column stores a time stamp when the alert was imported to a patient's Progress Notes. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: This column stores a flag 0 or 1. 1 - when the auto imported alert is removed manually and the removal is undone or when the alert is added manually, and then removed manually or 0 - otherwise.

columns.name: RemovedDate
columns.description: This column stores a time stamp when the auto imported alert was removed manually. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

columns.name: orderStatusIndicator
columns.description: This column is linked to the LastDoneDate column. This column stores 0, 1 or 2. 0 - There is no order. 1 -  There is a test is ordered, 2- There is a test received.

table_description: This table stores information about patients' allergies, including the drug causing the allergy, the type of allergy, and its status.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a patient whose allergies are being documented. This column refers to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: drug
columns.description: This column stores the name of the allergen causing the allergy to the patient.

columns.name: allergy
columns.description: This column stores the reaction for the corresponding allergy.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores the id of an encounter for which allergies are being documented. This column refers to the encounterid column in the enc table.

columns.name: itemid
columns.description: This column stores the itemid of an allergen causing the allergy to the patient. This column refers to the itemid column in the items table.

columns.name: displayIndex
columns.description: This column stores the order in which allergies are displayed in the user interface.

columns.name: SMDamConceptid
columns.description: This column stores the order in which allergies are displayed in the user interface.

columns.name: SMDamConceptidDesc
columns.description: This column is not being used.

columns.name: ndc_code
columns.description: This column stores the National Drug Code (NDC) for an allergen causing allergy to the patient.

columns.name: allergytype
columns.description: This column stores the type of allergy.  Example: Allergy, Side Effects, Contraindication, Lack of Therapeutic Effect.

columns.name: type
columns.description: This column stores char values to indicate whether allergies are structured/coded or unstructured/uncoded.  1 - structured/coded allergy, 2 - unstructured/uncoded allergy.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores information whether the patient is still allergic to an allergen. Two statuses are stored in this column 'Active' or 'Inactive'. By default, it is set to 'Active'.

columns.name: criticality
columns.description: This column stores criticality of allergy (e.g., High, Low, Medium).

columns.name: onsetdate
columns.description: This column stores the date when allergic reaction to a allergen started for a patient. Date is stored in DD/MM/YYYY format.

table_description: This table stores data imported from the EHX server when a user imports allergies for a patient. This table is populated when the local database does not have allergies.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is an auto-incremented primary key in this column.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a patient's encounter from which data is being imported. This column refers to the encounterid column in the enc table.

columns.name: trUserid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a user who imported allergies related data from the EHX server. This column refer to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: AllergyName
columns.description: This column stores the name of the allergan being imported from the EHX server.

columns.name: reaction
columns.description: This column stores the patient's reaction to the allergy imported from the EHX server.

columns.name: MappedAllergyName
columns.description: When imported allergies are mapped using itemid, this column stores the name of the equivalent allergy mapped with the allergies from the items table. The mapping is performed by the end user.

columns.name: mtimestamp
columns.description: This column stores the date and time when the record was imported from the EHX server.

columns.name: hasMatched
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the imported allergies has been matched with a local database or not. 0 - has matched, or 1 - not matched.

columns.name: delflag
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the record has been marked as deleted or not. 0  - Record is NOT marked as deleted, or 1 - Record is marked as deleted.

columns.name: CCRDataObjectid
columns.description: This column stores an id received in CCR document for each allergy listed in the CCR. This column stores a unique number for each allergy imported in a single call from the EHX server.

columns.name: refReqid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a referral in case allergy related information has been imported using the RCP > DRTLA tab. This column refers to the Referralid column in the referral table.

columns.name: allergyType
columns.description: This column stores the type of allergy whether it is coded or uncoded.

columns.name: mappedAllergyItemid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the equivalent item mapped with the items table. It is the itemid from the items table.

table_description: This table stores information about patients' allergy check-in details, including their encounter, facility, and any reactions or notes related to the check-in.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: PATIENTid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the patient. Foreign key relation to the patient table (e.g., `patient.id`). Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: ENCOUNTERid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the patient's encounter. Foreign key relation to the encounter table (e.g., `encounter.id`). Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: SHOT_FAC_TYPE
columns.description: A small integer representing the type of shot facility. Example: 0, 1, 2.

columns.name: FACILITYid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the facility where the check-in occurred. Example: 501, 502, 503.

columns.name: FACILITYNAME
columns.description: Name of the facility where the check-in occurred. Example: "Allergy Clinic A", "Allergy Clinic B".

columns.name: PT_CHKIN_STATUS
columns.description: A small integer representing the patient's check-in status. Example: 0 (not checked in), 1 (checked in).

columns.name: DELETEFLAG
columns.description: A small integer indicating whether the record has been deleted. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

columns.name: PT_ADMIN_STATUS
columns.description: A small integer representing the patient's administration status. Example: 0 (not administered), 1 (administered).

columns.name: DIS_CONDITION
columns.description: A string describing the patient's condition at the discharge. Example: "Mild allergy", "Severe allergy".

columns.name: DIS_IS_PATIENT_WAITED
columns.description: A small integer indicating whether the patient waited during the check-in. Example: 0 (no), 1 (yes).

columns.name: DIS_REASON
columns.description: A string describing the reason for the patient's discharge. Example: "Routine check-up", "Allergic reaction".

columns.name: DIS_NOTES
columns.description: A string containing any additional notes related to the patient's discharge: "Patient was anxious", "Patient had a mild reaction".

columns.name: NA_REASON
columns.description: A string describing the reason for not administering the shot. Example: "Patient refused", "Medical contraindication".

columns.name: IS_SYS_REACTION
columns.description: A small integer indicating whether there was a systemic reaction. Example: 0 (no), 1 (yes).

columns.name: SYS_REACTION
columns.description: A string describing the systemic reaction, if any. Example: "Anaphylaxis", "Urticaria".

columns.name: SYS_REACTION_TIME
columns.description: The date and time when the systemic reaction occurred. Example: "2021-08-01 14:30:00".

columns.name: SYS_NOTES
columns.description: A string containing any additional notes related to the systemic reaction. Example: "Patient was treated with epinephrine", "Reaction resolved within 30 minutes".

columns.name: SYS_USERid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the user who recorded the systemic reaction. Example: 10001, 10002, 10003.

columns.name: SYS_USERNAME
columns.description: The username of the user who recorded the systemic reaction. Example: "userA", "userB".

columns.name: DIS_TIME
columns.description: The date and time when the patient was discharged. Example: "2021-08-01 15:00:00".

columns.name: DIS_USERid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the user who recorded the patient's discharge. Example: 10001, 10002, 10003.

columns.name: DIS_USERNAME
columns.description: The username of the user who recorded the patient's discharge. Example: "userA", "userB".

columns.name: SHOT_ADMIN_TIME
columns.description: The date and time when the shot was administered. Example: "2021-08-01 14:00:00".

table_description: This table stores the mapping information of allergy elements, including their categories and parent items.

columns.name: id
columns.description: The column stores an id of the elements (allergen items) mapping with forms. This is an auto incremental primary key of This column .

columns.name: FORMid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of a form, which is associated with elements (allergen items). It refers to column formid from allergy_form table.

columns.name: CATid
columns.description: This column stores id of the category which is associated with the form. It refers to column itemid from items table.

columns.name: CATNAME
columns.description: This column stores name of the category which is associated with the form. It refers to column itemName from items table.

columns.name: ITEMid
columns.description: This column stores id of the item which is associated with the category. It refers to column itemid from items table.

columns.name: ITEMNAME
columns.description: This column stores name of the item which is associated with the category. It refers to column itemName from items table.

columns.name: PARENTITEMid
columns.description: This column stores parentid of the item (in case of child allergens) which is associated with the child item. It refers to column itemid from items table.

table_description: This table stores information related to billing for allergy extracts, including patient details, insurance information, and billing status.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

columns.name: PATIENTid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the patient associated with the billing record. Foreign key referring to the `id` column in the `patients` table.

columns.name: QUEUEid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the queue associated with the billing record.

columns.name: ENCid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the encounter associated with the billing record.

columns.name: LABid

columns.name: MIXFACid

columns.name: INSid

columns.name: INSNAME

columns.name: FIRSTSHOTDATE

table_description: This table stores billing notes related to allergy extracts for each patient.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BYid
columns.description: identifier for the user who last updated the record. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in a `users` table. Example: 201, 202, 203.

table_description: This table stores information about allergy extracts and their associated ICD codes.

columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which is an auto-incrementing integer value. It uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Reportid
columns.description: This column stores id of past lab ordered for patient. This column refers to reportid column in labdata table.

columns.name: AttachedToEncid
columns.description: This column stores id of an encounter to which patient's past lab report is pulled to from Right Chart Panel. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the past report is marked as deleted or not. 0 -  Past order is not marked as deleted, 1 - Past order is marked as deleted.

columns.name: labAttributes
columns.description: This column stores date and time when lab result is merged to Progress Notes from Right Chart Panel. Date and time are stores in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.000 format.

columns.name: performedDate
columns.description: This column stores date and time when lab result is merged to Progress Notes from Right Chart Panel. Date and time are stores in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.000 format.

table_description: This table stores a list of past PPD tests pulled into current Progress Notes from the RCP (Right Chart Panel). This table stores the ImmunizationId and the EncounterID if a PPD type of Immunization Order has been pulled into an encounter to document readings.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is auto incremented primary key in this column.

columns.name: ImmInjId
columns.description: This column stores id of past test/immunization administered to the patient when the record is pulled to current Progress Notes from Right Chart Panel. This column refer to immunizationid column in immunizations table.

columns.name: AttachedToEncId
columns.description: This column stores id of an encounter to which patient's past immunization test/immunization is pulled to from Right Chart Panel. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the record  has been marked as deleted or not. 0 - Immunization test has NOT been removed from Progress Notes, 1 - Immunization test has been removed from Progress Notes.

table_description: This table stores occupational medicine hearing test data for employees, including exposure levels, test dates, and related information.

columns.name: OccMedid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each occupational medicine hearing test record. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: identifier for the encounter associated with the hearing test. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: testDate
columns.description: Date and time when the hearing test was conducted. Example: '2021-08-01 14:30:00'.

columns.name: exposureLevelInHours
columns.description: Number of hours the employee was exposed to noise. Example: 8, 12, 16.

columns.name: exposureLevelInDb
columns.description: Noise exposure level in decibels (dB) the employee was exposed to. Example: 85, 90, 95.

columns.name: chartData
columns.description: A string containing chart data related to the hearing test. Example: '1,2,3;4,5,6;7,8,9'.

columns.name: retestDate
columns.description: Date when a retest is scheduled, if applicable. Example: '2021-08-15'.

columns.name: reviewedByid
columns.description: identifier for the user who reviewed the hearing test results. Foreign key relation to `users` table, `UID` column. Example: 5, 6, 7.

columns.name: examinedByid
columns.description: identifier for the user who examined the employee during the hearing test. Foreign key relation to `users` table, `UID` column. Example: 8, 9, 10.

columns.name: educationProvidedDate
columns.description: Date when education was provided to the employee regarding hearing protection. Example: '2021-08-02'.

columns.name: employeeTrainedDate
columns.description: Date when the employee was trained on hearing protection. Example: '2021-08-03'.

columns.name: scheduledDate
columns.description: Date when the hearing test was scheduled. Example: '2021-07-31'.

columns.name: recordUpdated
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the record has been updated (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: recordCreatedDate
columns.description: Date and time when the hearing test record was created. Example: '2021-07-30 10:00:00'.

columns.name: recordModifiedDate
columns.description: Date and time when the hearing test record was last modified, if applicable. Example: '2021-08-01 16:00:00'.

columns.name: structureDataid
columns.description: identifier for the structure data related to the hearing test. Foreign key relation to `structaudiology` table, `structureDataid` column. Example: 20, 21, 22.

columns.name: calibrationdate
columns.description: Date when the hearing test equipment was last calibrated. Example: '2021-07-01'.

columns.name: Empid
columns.description: identifier for the employee who underwent the hearing test. Foreign key relation to `employment_history` table, `id` column. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

table_description: This table stores logs of additional hours for patients, including information about the patient, the CPT item, bonus hours, the user who modified the log, and the authorization number.

columns.description: Unique identifier for each log entry. It is an integer value and is the primary key for the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.description: identifier for the patient associated with the log entry. It is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `patients` table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: cptitemid
columns.description: It is a foreign key that refers to the id column in the items table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: bonushoursid

columns.description: It is a foreign key that refers to the id column in the user table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

table_description: This table stores confidential notes related to patients, created by specific users.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key, an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each confidential note in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This is a foreign key relation (references `users` table's `UID` column) and an integer that represents the unique identifier of the patient associated with the confidential note. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: This is a foreign key relation (references `users` table's `UID` column) and an integer that represents the unique identifier of the user who created the confidential note. Example: 201, 202, 203, etc.

columns.name: name
columns.description: This is a varchar(50) column that stores the name or title of the confidential note. Example: "Medical History", "Allergies", "Surgery Details", etc.

columns.name: note
columns.description: This is a text column that stores the content of the confidential note. Example: "Patient has a history of asthma and needs to avoid certain medications."

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the confidential note was created. Example: "2021-09-01 12:34:56"

columns.name: modifiedDatetime
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the confidential note was last modified. Example: "2021-09-02 14:30:00"

columns.name: delflag
columns.description: This is a tinyint(1) column that stores a boolean value (0 or 1) to indicate whether the confidential note has been deleted (soft delete). A value of 0 means the note is not deleted, and a value of 1 means the note is deleted. Example: 0, 1

columns.description: This column stores value of billingdata id.

columns.name: endtime

table_description: This table stores the mapping between DAP encounters and program enrollments done for a patient.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key of the table, which is an auto-incrementing integer value that uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `encounterid` column in the `enc` table. It represents the id of the encounter associated with the program. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: ptAcoid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `ptacoprograms` table. It represents the id of the program associated with the encounter. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint(1) column that indicates whether the mapping has been deleted or not. A value of '0' means the mapping is not deleted, and a value of '1' means the mapping is deleted. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores information about various groups.

columns.name: groupid
columns.description: This is the primary key and a unique identifier for each group. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: groupName
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the name of the group. It is a required field and cannot be NULL. Example: "Group A", "Group B", "Group C", etc.

columns.name: inactive
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the group is inactive or not. It has a default value of '0', where '0' means active and '1' means inactive. Example: 0 (active), 1 (inactive).

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the group has been deleted or not. It has a default value of '0', where '0' means not deleted and '1' means deleted. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

columns.name: downloadFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the group has been downloaded or not. It has a default value of '0', where '0' means not downloaded and '1' means downloaded. Example: 0 (not downloaded), 1 (downloaded).

table_description: This table stores information about triggers related to care plans, such as review days, patient sign-off days, and utilization days.

columns.description: Unique identifier for each care plan trigger entry. Example: 1, 2, 3

columns.name: CarePlanid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the care plan associated with the trigger. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `careplans` table. Example: 101, 102, 103

columns.name: ReviewDays
columns.description: Number of days after which the care plan should be reviewed. Example: 30, 60, 90

columns.name: ReviewRepeat
columns.description: Indicates whether the review process should be repeated (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1

columns.name: PtSignOffDays
columns.description: Number of days after which the patient should sign off on the care plan. Example: 7, 14, 21

columns.name: PtSignOffRepeat
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient sign-off process should be repeated (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1

columns.name: UtilizationDays
columns.description: Number of days after which the care plan utilization should be checked. Example: 15, 30, 45

columns.name: UtilizationRepeat
columns.description: Indicates whether the utilization check process should be repeated (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1

table_description: This table stores the addendums or additional information related to care plan reviews, along with the user who added the addendum and the date it was added.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which uniquely identifies each addendum entry. It is an integer value that auto-increments with each new entry. For example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: reviewid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the care plan review to which the addendum is related. It is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `careplanreviews` table. For example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: addendum
columns.description: This column stores the text content of the addendum. It is a mandatory field and can store large amounts of text. For example: "Additional notes on patient's progress", "Updated medication list", etc.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the user who added the addendum. It is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `users` table. For example: 1001, 1002, 1003, etc.

columns.name: DATE
columns.description: This column stores the date and time when the addendum was added. It is a datetime value. For example: '2021-09-01 12:34:56', '2021-09-02 14:30:00', etc.

table_description: This table stores information about various codes, their names, and their associated alphanumeric and numeric identifiers.

columns.name: Code
columns.description: This is the primary key column and contains a unique varchar(15) code value. For example, 'A123B'.

columns.name: Name
columns.description: This column stores the text description or name associated with the code. For example, 'Sample Code Name'.

columns.name: Alphaid
columns.description: This column stores the value which may be NULL or 1st Character of Code i.e. if  code is number then default value NULL or code is A1,A2,A3,A4 then stores A.

columns.name: Numid
columns.description: This column stores the default value 0 or the code i.e. if code is numeric value then stores the same numeric value otherwise if code is A0,A1 then 0,1.

table_description: This table stores the mapping between cases and care teams, including information about the primary care team, role, care type, and the relationship with the COC table.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the case_careteam_map table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: caseid
columns.description: identifier for the case associated with the care team. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: careteamid
columns.description: identifier for the care team associated with the case. Example: 201, 202, 203.

columns.name: isprimary
columns.description: A boolean flag indicating if the care team is the primary team for the case. 1 represents true (primary), and 0 represents false (not primary). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: role
columns.description: identifier for the role of the care team in the case. Example: 301, 302, 303.

columns.name: delflag
columns.description: A boolean flag indicating if the record has been deleted. 1 represents true (deleted), and 0 represents false (not deleted). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: caretype
columns.description: A string representing the type of care provided by the care team. Example: 'emergency', 'routine', 'specialist'.

columns.name: coc_id
columns.description: identifier for the coc (Chain of Custody) record associated with the case_careteam_map. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `coc` table. Example: 401, 402, 403.

table_description: This table stores information about different cases, including details about the patient, provider, guarantor, attorney, case manager, insurance, and other related information.

columns.name: Caseid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each case (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the patient associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `patients` table (e.g., 101, 102, 103).

columns.name: Providerid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the provider associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `Doctors` table (e.g., 201, 202, 203).

columns.name: Guarantorid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the guarantor associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `patients` table (e.g., 301, 302, 303).

columns.name: Attorneyid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the attorney associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `patient_attorney` table (e.g., 401, 402, 403).

columns.name: CaseManagerid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the case manager associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `casemanager` table (e.g., 501, 502, 503).

columns.name: Insuranceid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the insurance associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `insurance` table (e.g., 601, 602, 603).

columns.name: CaseType
columns.description: Integer representing the type of case,  foreign key referring to the `case_types` table (e.g., 1 for personal injury, 2 for workers' compensation).

columns.name: BillToPatient
columns.description: Integer indicating whether the bill should be sent to the patient (1 for yes, 0 for no).

columns.name: PreAuth
columns.description: Pre-authorization information for the case (e.g., 'PA12345').

columns.name: Referral
columns.description: Referral information for the case (e.g., 'Dr. Smith').

columns.name: CourtName
columns.description: Name of the court associated with the case (e.g., 'Superior Court').

columns.name: CourtLocation
columns.description: Location of the court associated with the case (e.g., 'Los Angeles, CA').

columns.name: CourtCase
columns.description: Court case number (e.g., 'LA123456').

columns.name: CourtDate
columns.description: Date of the court hearing (e.g., '2022-01-01').

columns.name: DateOfInjury
columns.description: Date of the injury related to the case (e.g., '2021-12-01').

columns.name: WorkRelated
columns.description: Integer indicating whether the case is work-related (1 for yes, 0 for no).

columns.name: Accident
columns.description: Integer indicating whether the case involves an accident (1 for yes, 0 for no).

columns.name: AccidentState
columns.description: Two-letter state abbreviation where the accident occurred (e.g., 'CA').

columns.name: AccidentTime
columns.description: Time of the accident (e.g., '14:30').

columns.name: AccidentCause
columns.description: Cause of the accident (e.g., 'Slip and fall').

columns.name: MissedWorkFrom
columns.description: Start date of missed work due to the injury (e.g., '2021-12-02').

columns.name: MissedWorkTo
columns.description: End date of missed work due to the injury (e.g., '2021-12-15').

columns.name: HospitalizationFrom
columns.description: Start date of hospitalization due to the injury (e.g., '2021-12-01').

columns.name: HospitalizationTo
columns.description: End date of hospitalization due to the injury (e.g., '2021-12-05').

columns.name: city
columns.description: City where the case is located (e.g., 'Los Angeles').

columns.name: county
columns.description: County where the case is located (e.g., 'Los Angeles County').

columns.name: AddressNoStNo
columns.description: Address number and street number of the case location (e.g., '123 Main St').

columns.name: DescAccOccur
columns.description: Description of how the accident occurred (e.g., 'Slipped on wet floor').

columns.name: externalCaseNo
columns.description: External case number, if applicable (e.g., 'EXT12345').

columns.name: empDetailid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the employee detail associated with the case, foreign key referring to the `employee_details` table (e.g., 701, 702, 703).

columns.name: addressline1
columns.description: First line of the case address (e.g., '123 Main St').

columns.name: addressline2
columns.description: Second line of the case address, if applicable (e.g., 'Apt 4B').

columns.name: zipcode
columns.description: Zip code of the case location (e.g., '90001').

table_description: This table stores information about insurance cases, including their associated case and insurance IDs, display index, and insurance details ID.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and is an auto-incrementing integer value. It uniquely identifies each record in the `case_insurances` table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Caseid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in another table (e.g., `cases` table) and represents the case associated with the insurance record. It is an integer value and is set to 0 by default. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: Insid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the insurance patient has. This column refers to column insid from insurance table.

columns.name: displayIndex
columns.description: This column stores a digit to indicate order in which insurance records should be listed in user interface.

columns.name: insurancedetid
columns.description: This column stores the id of the insurance detail of the patient's insurance. This column refers to column id from insurancedetail table.

table_description: This table is used to store the information about the patient's case.

columns.name: CaseId
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and uniquely identifies each case. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented for each new case. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: CaseName
columns.description: Case_management_CaseName Column store Case Label value from Billing (Band) -> Case Management -> View Case Detail Screen.  Example : "Motor Vehicle Case" OR "Accident Case"

columns.name: CreatedBy
columns.description: This is an integer column that stores the user ID of the person who created the case. It is a required field and has a default value of 0. This column can be a foreign key referring to the user ID in a `users` table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: AssignedTo
columns.description: This column stores the id of the Provider/Staff to whom case is assigned. This column refers to column uid from user table.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This is an integer column that indicates whether the case has been deleted or not. It is a required field and has a default value of 0. A value of 0 means the case is not deleted, and a value of 1 means the case is deleted. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: Status
columns.description: This column stores the value 0/1 to indicate if this is an ongoing case. 0 - Case is Open , 1 - Case is Closed.

table_description: This table stores information about different types of cases.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column that uniquely identifies each case type. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits and is automatically incremented. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Code
columns.description: This column stores a unique code for each case type. It is a string with a maximum length of 10 characters and has a default value of an empty string. Example: 'CT001', 'CT002', 'CT003', etc.

columns.name: Name
columns.description: This column stores the name of the case type. It is a string with a maximum length of 255 characters and has a default value of an empty string. Example: 'Criminal', 'Civil', 'Family', etc.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: This column indicates whether a case type has been deleted or not. It is an integer with a maximum length of 2 digits and has a default value of '0'. A value of '0' means the case type is not deleted, and a value of '1' means the case type is deleted. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores additional details related to a specific case, such as disability dates, employer note dates, and return to duty dates.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which is an integer value that uniquely identifies each record. It is an auto-incrementing value. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: caseid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `CaseId` column in the `case_details` table. It represents the unique identifier of the case that the additional details are associated with. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: disabilitybegundate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the disability associated with the case began. Example: '2021-09-01 10:30:00'

columns.name: employernotedate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the employer provided a note related to the case. Example: '2021-09-02 14:45:00'

columns.name: disabilityenddate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the disability associated with the case ended. Example: '2021-09-30 18:00:00'

columns.name: modifiedbegandate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the modified disability period began, if applicable. Example: '2021-09-15 09:00:00'

columns.name: modifiedenddate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the modified disability period ended, if applicable. Example: '2021-09-29 17:00:00'

columns.name: returndutydate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the individual returned to duty after the disability period. Example: '2021-10-01 08:00:00'

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that stores a boolean value (0 or 1) indicating whether the row has been deleted or not. A value of 0 means the row is not deleted, and a value of 1 means the row is deleted. Example: 0 or 1

table_description: This table stores information about case managers, including their personal details, contact information, and preferences.

columns.name: Id
columns.description: This column stores id of case manager. It is auto increment primary key. It defines identifier of case manager.

columns.name: lname
columns.description: Last name of the case manager (e.g., Smith, Johnson, Williams).

columns.name: fname
columns.description: First name of the case manager (e.g., John, Jane, Michael).

columns.name: address1
columns.description: First line of the case manager's address (e.g., 123 Main St, 456 Oak St).

columns.name: address2
columns.description: Second line of the case manager's address, if applicable (e.g., Apt 4B, Suite 200).

columns.name: city
columns.description: City where the case manager is located (e.g., New York, Los Angeles, Chicago).

columns.name: State
columns.description: Two-letter abbreviation of the state where the case manager is located (e.g., NY, CA, IL).

columns.name: Zip
columns.description: Zip code of the case manager's address (e.g., 10001, 90001, 60601).

columns.name: Email
columns.description: Email address of the case manager (e.g., john.smith@example.com, jane.johnson@example.com).

columns.name: Phone
columns.description: Phone number of the case manager (e.g., (555) 123-4567, (555) 987-6543).

columns.name: Fax
columns.description: Fax number of the case manager, if applicable (e.g., (555) 123-4568, (555) 987-6544).

columns.name: ContactPreference
columns.description: Preferred method of contact for the case manager (e.g., Email, Phone, Fax).

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: Additional notes or comments about the case manager (e.g., "Prefers morning calls", "On vacation until 10/15").

columns.name: Dob
columns.description: Date of birth of the case manager (e.g., 1980-01-01, 1990-12-31).

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: A flag indicating if the case manager's record has been deleted (0 for not deleted, 1 for deleted).

columns.name: EnterpriseId
columns.description: Unique identifier for the enterprise the case manager belongs to. This can be a foreign key referring to the `Id` column in another table, such as an `enterprise` table.
