table_description: This table stores information about different alert codes and their descriptions used in PHM Billing to show an alert to the user.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT (11). This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions over the years hence integer(Range: 0-2,147,483,647) is selected. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index.

columns.name: alertCode
columns.description: Contains unique alert code which are used in PHM Billing in case if there is an alert for a patient while claim/encounter generation. The data type of this column is vatchar(12).

columns.name: alertDesc
columns.description: Contains desctiption of the alert which are used in PHM Billing in case if there is an alert for a patient while claim/encounter generation. The data type of this column is vatchar(255).

columns.name: delFlag
columns.description: Flag indicates if this data is deleted or not, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores binary flag i.e 0/1. 0: not deleted 1: deleted - By default the record must not be in deleted status hence default 0 is chosen.

table_description: This table stores information about PHM Billing batch process including batch date, last run batch date, success, failure, do not create, total  and alerts. It stores information about created and modified date time. Each month / year pair will have only one entry in ccm_batch table.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT (11). This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions over the years hence integer(Range: 0-2,147,483,647) is selected. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index.

columns.name: success
columns.description: Contains total number of successful patients for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: failure
columns.description: Contains total number of failed patients for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: doNotCreateClaim
columns.description: Contains total number of patients for which the user has selected Do Not Create Claim option for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Contains total number of patients for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: createClaims
columns.description: Contains total number of patients for which the user has selected Do Not Create Claim option earlier and now the user has added them back to reprocess queue for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: delFlag
columns.description: Flag indicates if this data is deleted or not, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores binary flag i.e 0/1. 0: not deleted 1: deleted - By default the record must not be in deleted status hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Contains current status of PHM Billing batch process. The allowed values are 1, 2 and 3. 1 indicates Run, 2 for Generate and 3 is for Complete. The data type of this column is tinyint.

columns.name: lastUpdatedUID
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a user which references the UID column of the user table. It refers to the user who modified the record last. The data type chosen is INT. This column does not allow a NULL value.

columns.name: alert
columns.description: Contains total number of patients who have alerts for PHM Billing batch process of a billing month. The data type of this column is INT. The value of this column cannot be NULL, hence it has a default value of 0.

columns.name: batchDate
columns.description: Contains the month for which the batch is run.  The datatype of this field is datetime. This field does not allow NULL values.

columns.name: lastBatchRunDt
columns.description: Contains the date when the batch was last run by a user for specific billing month. The datatype of this field is datetime. This field does not allow NULL values.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Contains text notes added by the user when phm billing batch is processed. The data type of this field is TEXT. This field allows a NULL value.

columns.name: createdDtTime
columns.description: Contains the date and time when the batch was first run by a user for specific billing month. The datatype of this field is datetime. This field does allows a NULL value.

columns.name: modifiedDtTime
columns.description: Contains the date and time when the batch record was last modified by a user for specific billing month. The datatype of this field is datetime. This field  allows a NULL value.

table_description: This table stores information about missed claims in a batch process, including details about the patient, batch, and error codes.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT (11). This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions over the years hence integer(Range: 0-2,147,483,647) is selected. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: Contains Primary Key column of user table to store Patient id. The value of this field cannot be NULL.

columns.name: batchid
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a ccm batch which references the id column of the ccm_batch table. It refers to the batch of specific billing month. The data type chosen is INT. This column does not allow a NULL value.

columns.name: batchLogid
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a ccm batch log which references the id column of the ccm_batch_log table. It refers to the batch log of specific billing month. The data type chosen is INT. This column does not allow a NULL value.

columns.name: ptacoid
columns.description: Contains Primary Key column of ptacoprograms table to store PTACO id . The datatype chosen is an INT  The value of this field cannot be NULL.

columns.name: claimid
columns.description: When batch is processed and claim is generated , the claim id is stored in this column. This field can not have a NULL value. The default value of this field is 0. The data type chosen is INT as this field is pointing to id column of edi_invoice table which is also int.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: When batch is processed and encounter is generated , the encounter id is stored in this column. This field can not have a NULL value. The default value of this field is 0. references to  to encounterid column of enc table. The data type chosen is INT as this field is pointing to encounterid column of enc table which is also int.

columns.name: alertid
columns.description: This is alert id which references to id column of ccm_alerts table. This field contains alert description in case if there is an alert in claim generation. The data type of this field is INT. This field cannot have a NULL value.

columns.name: errorCodeid
columns.description: This is error id which references to id column of ccm_errorcode table. This field contains error description in case if claim generation failed for a patient because of validation or some other issue. The data type of this field is INT. This field cannot have a NULL value.

columns.name: claimDate
columns.description: Contains date time when the batch is processed. The data type of this field is datetime. This field can have a NULL value.

columns.name: BillingDate
columns.description: Contains date of specific billing month for which the batch is processed. The data type of this field is datetime. This field can not have a NULL value.

columns.name: delFlag
columns.description: Flag indicates if this data is deleted or not, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores binary flag i.e 0/1. 0: not deleted 1: deleted - By default the record must not be in deleted status hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: addedDateTime
columns.description: Contains the date and time when the batch was run by a user for specific billing month. The datatype of this field is datetime. This field does allows a NULL value.

columns.name: modDateTime
columns.description: Contains the date and time when the batch was last modified by a user for specific billing month. The datatype of this field is datetime. This field  allows a NULL value.

table_description: This table stores information about batch processing result of each billing eligible patient in PHM programs. It stores information related to program enrolled in, CPT Code, CPT Units, claimId, encounterId billing date.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT (11). This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions over the years hence integer(Range: 0-2,147,483,647) is selected. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index.

columns.name: batchid
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a ccm batch which references the id column of the ccm_batch table. It refers to the batch of specific billing month. The data type chosen is INT. This column does not allow a NULL value.

columns.name: batchLogid

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: Contains Primary Key column of user table to store Patient id. The value of this field cannot be NULL.

columns.name: ptacoid
columns.description: Contains Primary Key column of ptacoprograms table to store PTACO id . The datatype chosen is an INT  The value of this field cannot be NULL.

columns.name: ccm_99490

table_description: This table stores information about time added by staff / provider for a ccm / cpo / rpm enrolled patient including start time, end time, duration, reason, notes, recorded manualy or by timer, user who added time.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT. This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions added. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index

columns.name: PTCO_id
columns.description: This column is used to identify enrollment details of patient. This is foreign key column. It refers to primary key of ptacoprograms table. Data type is int(11).

columns.name: Patient_id
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a Patient which references the UID column of the user table. The data type chosen is INT. This column allows a NULL value.

columns.name: START_TIMER
columns.description: Contains date time when the timer was started and datatype is DATETIME. This column store datetime hence time stamp is selected.

columns.name: END_TIMER
columns.description: Contains date time when the timer was ended and datatype is DATETIME. This column store datetime hence time stamp is selected.

columns.name: DURATION
columns.description: Contains duration for which the timer was running and datatype is DATETIME. This column store duration hence time stamp is selected.

columns.name: REASON
columns.description: Contains the name of the timer reason and the data type is VARCHAR.Since the length of timer reasons would not exceed 255 characters it is selected as VARCHAR(255).

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: Contains the timer notes and the data type is TEXT.

columns.name: CreatedDateTime
columns.description: Contains date time when the timer record was created and datatype is DATETIME. This column store datetime hence time stamp is selected.

columns.name: RecordedManually
columns.description: Flag indicates is time is recorded manually or automaically by timer, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores integer value hence integer is selected. 0:Not manually recorded 1: Manually recorded. By default time is automatically recorded by timer hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: ReasonItemid
columns.description: Contains the itemid of the timer reason and datatype is INT. It refers the 'itemid' of items table. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL.

columns.name: loggedProviderid
columns.description: Contains the user id who was logged in when record was added or last updated  and datatype is INT. It refers the 'UID' of user table. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: Flag indicates reason has been deleted or not, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores integer value hence integer is selected. Datatype can be changed to tinyint - 0:NotDeleted 1: Deleted. By default timer record must not be in delete status hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: timerstatus
columns.description: Flag indicates is timer is running for the patient, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores integer value hence integer is selected. 0:Not running 1: Timer is running. By default timer is not automatically running hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: modDateTime
columns.description: Contains date time when the record was last modified and datatype is DATETIME. This column store datetime hence time stamp is selected.

columns.name: proffessionalTime
columns.description: Flag indicates is time is added by provider for the patient, datatype is TINYINT. This column stores integer value hence integer is selected. 0:Not added by provider 1: Added by Provider. By default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: finalBillingModule
columns.description: This column stores the program name incase of CCM RPM concurrent billing. This field indicates that specific timer entry should be allocated to which program. The data type is varchar(50). This column allows NULL value.

columns.name: billingProcessDone
columns.description: Flag indicates whether the cpt code decision is done considering this specific timer entry. Values 0 - billing process not done, 1 - billing process done. The data type is TINYINT. This column does not allow NULL value.

table_description: This table stores information about claims and their corresponding statuses, along with inbound and outbound messages related to the claims.

columns.name: id

columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the unique identifier for a claim. It has a maximum length of 20 characters and cannot be NULL. Example: 'CLM12345', 'CLM67890'.

columns.name: InBound277
columns.description: This is a text column that stores the inbound message related to the claim. Example: 'Inbound message for claim CLM12345'.

columns.name: CreatedDate
columns.description: This is a time stamp column that stores the date and time when the record was created or last updated. It is set to the current time stamp by default and updates automatically when the record is modified. Example: '2021-08-01 12:34:56'.

columns.name: ClaimStatusCode
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the status code of the claim. It has a maximum length of 25 characters and can be NULL. Example: 'PENDING', 'APPROVED', 'DENIED'.

columns.name: ClaimStatusid
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the unique identifier for the claim status. It has a maximum length of 10 characters and can be NULL. Example: 'ST1', 'ST2', 'ST3'.

columns.name: ClaimStatusCategory
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the category of the claim status. It has a maximum length of 10 characters and can be NULL. Example: 'CAT1', 'CAT2', 'CAT3'.

columns.name: Userid
columns.description: This is an integer column that stores the unique identifier of the user who created or modified the claim record. It can be NULL. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in a `users` table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: OutBound276
columns.description: This is a text column that stores the outbound message related to the claim. Example: 'Outbound message for claim CLM12345'.

columns.name: insid
columns.description: This is an integer column that stores the unique identifier of the insurance company related to the claim. It can be NULL. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in an `insurance` table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

table_description: This table stores information about different types of alerts, their descriptions, and various flags to indicate their properties and visibility.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which stores a unique integer value for each alert type. For example, 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: alerttype
columns.description: This column stores a short string (varchar) representing the type of alert. For example, "TFLEX", "AFLEX", "TATEX", etc.

columns.name: description
columns.description: This column stores a longer string (varchar) that provides a brief description of the alert type. For example, "System warning", "Data error", "Informational message", etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the alert type has been deleted or not. A value of '0' means the alert type is not deleted, and a value of '1' means it is deleted.

columns.name: alertCategory
columns.description: This column stores a short string (varchar) representing the category of the alert. For example, "system", "data", "user", etc.

columns.name: isActivePractiveView
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the alert type is active in the Practice View or not. A value of '0' means the alert type is not active, and a value of '1' means it is active.

columns.name: isActiveRPView
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the alert type is active in the RP View or not. A value of '0' means the alert type is not active, and a value of '1' means it is active.

columns.name: isAdvanced
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the alert type is considered advanced or not. A value of '0' means the alert type is not advanced, and a value of '1' means it is advanced.

table_description: This table stores information about claim alert files, including their import date, the user who imported them, and the contents of the files in JSON format.

columns.name: fileid
columns.description: This is the primary key and an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each claim alert file. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: filetimefield
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the time field associated with the claim alert file. Example: "2021-08-01 12:34:56".

columns.name: importdate
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the claim alert file was imported into the system. Example: "2021-08-01 12:34:56".

columns.name: importedby
columns.description: This is an integer column that stores the id of the user who imported the claim alert file. It can be a foreign key referring to the user's id in a separate user table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: jsonstring
columns.description: This is a longtext column that stores the contents of the claim alert file in JSON format. Example: '{"claim_id": 123, "alert_type": "high_risk", "details": "This claim has a high risk of fraud."}'

table_description: This table stores information related to claim alerts, including the type of alert, payer ID, and other relevant details.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each claim alert record. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: invoiceid
columns.description: identifier for the invoice associated with the claim alert. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in an `invoices` table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: alerttype
columns.description: identifier for the type of claim alert. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in an `alert_types` table. Example: 1 (Missing Information), 2 (Incorrect Information), 3 (Rejected Claim).

columns.name: payerid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the payer associated with the claim alert. Example: 'PAYER123', 'PAYER456', 'PAYER789'.

columns.name: actiondays
columns.description: Number of days to take action on the claim alert. Example: 5, 10, 15.

columns.name: fileid
columns.description: identifier for the file associated with the claim alert. This could be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in a `files` table. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: alertresult
columns.description: Text description of the result of the claim alert. Example: 'Resolved', 'Pending', 'Rejected'.

columns.name: issubmitted
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the claim alert has been submitted (1) or not (0). Example: 0 (Not Submitted), 1 (Submitted).

columns.name: alerttext
columns.description: Brief text description of the claim alert. Example: 'Missing patient information', 'Incorrect billing code', 'Rejected due to duplicate claim'.

columns.name: ignoreComment
columns.description: Comment explaining why the claim alert is being ignored, if applicable. Example: 'Resolved internally', 'Duplicate alert', ''.

table_description: This table stores information of patient's dental PSR (Periodontal Screening and Recording) data which is used in the Dental Examination screen.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is auto-incremented primary key in This column . Unique id is assigned to each PSR exam when they are created using User Interface. It is defined as NOT NULL constraint.

columns.name: Providerid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of a provider while appointment is created. It refers to column UID from user table. It is defined as NOT NULL constraint.�

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of a patient, for whom the appointment is created. It refers to column pid from patients table. It is defined as NOT NULL constraint.�

columns.name: USection1
columns.description: This column stores Upper level section 1 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: USection2
columns.description: This column stores Upper level section 2 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: USection3
columns.description: This column stores Upper level section 3 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: LSection1
columns.description: This column stores Lower level section 1 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: LSection2
columns.description: This column stores Lower level section 2 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: LSection3
columns.description: This column stores Lower level section 3 value from PSR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: Pattern
columns.description: This column stores pattern value like LL or LR. It allows NULL value as default.

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: Additional notes about the exam. Example: "Patient has mild gingivitis", "Patient needs deep cleaning".

columns.name: ExamDate
columns.description: This column stores Exam Date of PSR. It is defined as NOT NULL constraint.

columns.name: StarMark
columns.description: This column stores star mark value of PSR sections like Usection1, Usection2, Usection3, Lsection1, Lsection2, Lsection3. This column allows '0#0#0#0#0#0#' as default value.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: Indicates if the record has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores all the basic information of dental recalls which is used in the Dental Recall configuration screen, and in the CDSS > Dental tab.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is auto-incremented primary key in This column . Unique id is assigned to each Dental Recall data when user create new recall(Generic or Patient Specific). It is defined as NOT NULL constraint.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: This column stores Name of Dental Recall (Associated dental item name).

columns.name: Itemid
columns.description: This column stores itemid of Dental Recall (Associated itemid column value on dentalitems table).

columns.name: LowerAge
columns.description: This column stores Lower Age value configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: LowerAgeFlag
columns.description: This column stores Lower Age Flag value (Y=Year and M = Month) configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: UpperAge
columns.description: This column stores Upper Age  value configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: UpperAgeFlag
columns.description: This column stores Upper Age Flag value (Y=Year and M = Month) configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: Frequency
columns.description: This column stores Frequency value configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: FrequencyFlag
columns.description: This column stores Frequency  Flag value (Y=Year and M = Month) configuration of Generic Recall.

columns.name: Gender
columns.description: The gender for which the dental recall is applicable. Example: "Male", "Female", "All".

columns.name: WebRef
columns.description: A reference to a web resource related to the dental recall. Example: "https://example.com/dental_recall_101".

columns.name: LastUpdated
columns.description: time stamp of when the dental recall record was last updated. Example: "2021-08-01 12:34:56".

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: Flag to indicate if the dental recall record has been deleted. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column  stores information of patient's details of dental Recalls for patient specific recalls only which is used in CDSS> Dental tab screen. For Generic recalls, Patient id  value=0.

columns.name: ProcButtonid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of proc Button id. It refers to column procButtonNum from ProcButton table. User can set this value using Procedure button field from Dental Recall Configuration screen.

columns.name: ProcButtonName
columns.description: This column stores name of proc Button. It refers to column itemName from Definition table. User can set this value using Procedure button field from Dental Recall Configuration screen.

columns.name: IsRecurrent
columns.description: Flag to indicate if the dental recall is recurrent. Example: 0 (not recurrent), 1 (recurrent).

columns.name: DueDate
columns.description: The date when the dental recall is due. Example: "2021-08-15", "2021-09-01".

columns.name: SuppressDate
columns.description: The date when the dental recall is suppressed. Example: "2021-08-10", "2021-09-05".

columns.name: SuppressFlg
columns.description: Flag to indicate if the dental recall is suppressed. Example: 0 (not suppressed), 1 (suppressed).

columns.name: SuppressNotes
columns.description: Notes related to the suppression of the dental recall. Example: "Patient requested postponement", "Rescheduled due to dentist's unavailability".

columns.name: addOneDay
columns.description: Flag to indicate if one day should be added to the due date. Example: 0 (do not add), 1 (add).

columns.name: PermanentSuppressFlg
columns.description: Flag to indicate if the dental recall is permanently suppressed. Example: 0 (not permanent), 1 (permanent).

table_description: This table stores historical information of dental recalls and this information is used to display in the Progress Notes > CDSS > Dental tab.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column  stores information of patient id for patient specific dental recalls which is used in CDSS> Dental tab screen.

columns.name: Recallid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of Dental Recalls. It refers to column id from dental_recall table.

columns.name: Procedureid
columns.description: This column stores identifier number of Procedure id. It refers to column procNum from ProcedureHistory table.

columns.name: LastDoneDate
columns.description: This column stores Last Done Date of Dental Recall.

columns.name: LastDoneBy
columns.description: This column stores user id value which indicates user details who Added historical information of Dental recall.

columns.name: UpdatedDate
columns.description: This column stores Updated Date of Dental Recall historical data.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the dental recall history record has been deleted. It is of tinyint(1) data type and has a default value of '0'. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

columns.name: RecallStatus
Itemid
columns.description: This column stores itemid of Dental Recall (Associated itemid column value on dentalitems table).

columns.name: DentalItemid
columns.description: This column stores dentalitemid of Dental Recall (Associated id column value on dentalitems table).

table_description: This table suppresses information of dental recalls and this information is used to display in the Progress Notes > CDSS > Dental tab.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each dental recall suppression record. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: DentalRecallid
columns.description: The identifier of the dental recall record that this suppression is associated with. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `dental_recall` table. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: SuppressDate
columns.description: The date when the dental recall suppression was created. Example: '2021-09-01', '2021-09-02', '2021-09-03'.

columns.name: SuppressFlg
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the dental recall is suppressed (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: SuppressNotes
columns.description: Text notes related to the dental recall suppression. Example: 'Patient requested a temporary hold on recalls', 'Moved out of state'.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores the patient ID for patient-specific dental recalls that are used on the CDSS > Dental window.

columns.name: SuppressBy
columns.description: The identifier of the user who created the dental recall suppression. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `user` table. Example: 2001, 2002, 2003.

columns.name: CreatedDate
columns.description: The date when the dental recall suppression record was created. Example: '2021-09-01', '2021-09-02', '2021-09-03'.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the dental recall suppression record is deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: PermanentSuppressFlg
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the dental recall suppression is permanent (1) or temporary (0). Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores information about dental appointment resource details, including provider time, resource time, chair time, and whether the appointment is for dental services or not.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented with each new record. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encid
columns.description: This column stores encounterid value. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: providerTime
columns.description: This column stores the time allocated for the provider during the appointment. It is a varchar(250) field that can store up to 250 characters. Example: [{"startValue":0,"endValue":10}]

columns.name: resourceTime
columns.description: This column stores the time allocated for resources (e.g., equipment, staff) during the appointment. It is a varchar(250) field that can store up to 250 characters. Example: [{"startValue":10,"endValue":20}]

columns.name: chairTime
columns.description: This column stores the time allocated for the dental chair during the appointment. It is a varchar(250) field that can store up to 250 characters. Example :[{"startValue":20,"endValue":30}]

columns.name: isDental
columns.description: This is a tinyint(1) column that indicates whether the appointment is for dental services (1) or not (0). Example: 1 (dental), 0 (non-dental).

table_description: This is the dictionary table for dental entry statuses. Every dental procedure documented will be in one of the statuses defined in this table.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each dental entry status. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits and is automatically incremented. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: entryStatus
columns.description: This column stores the status of the dental entry as a string with a maximum length of 20 characters. Example: 'Completed', 'Pending', 'Cancelled', etc.

columns.name: colorCode
columns.description: This column stores the color code associated with the dental entry status as a string with a maximum length of 10 characters. Example: '#FF5733', '#C70039', '#900C3F', etc.

columns.name: icon
columns.description: This column is currently unused and will be removed in a future build.

columns.name: displayImg
columns.description: This column is currently unused and will be removed in a future build.

columns.name: orderStatus
columns.description: This column represents the order of precedence given to the Entry Status when displaying procedures on the Progress Notes. The lower the value, the higher is the status (Example - status 1 is given precedence over status 3).

table_description: This table establishes the relationship between a group note and associated procedures. Each group note ID can be linked to two or more procNums, and there by, linking procedures to the group note. A group note is a single note that applies to multiple procedures.

columns.name: groupNoteid
columns.description: This column is a reference to ProcNum column of the table procedurehistory. It identifies an entry in procedurehistory that's flagged as a group note.

columns.name: procNum
columns.description: This column is a reference to ProcNum column of the table procedurehistory. It identifies an entry in procedurehistory that's associated to the group note identified by the column groupNoteid. For each groupNoteid, there are two or more entries for procNum. This links the group note to the procedures.

table_description: This is a child table of items, containing only those CPTs which are configured as dental CPTs. In other words, an entry in this table identifies the CPT associated as a dental CPT code. The table also associates the CPT with additional properties that do not normally apply to non-dental CPT codes.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column stores the id for the dental CPT or procedure code. It is the auto-increment primary key column for the table.

columns.name: itemid
columns.description: This column references the column itemid of the table items for the dental CPT code. The dental CPTs are first created the same way as any other CPT codes with an entry in the table 'items'. They are flagged as dental codes when there is an entry for that itemid in This column .

columns.name: categoryid
columns.description: This is a reference to the id column dentalitemcategory table. It represents the category to which the dental CPT belongs.

columns.name: treatmentAreaid
columns.description: This is a reference to the id column dentaltreatmentarea table. It represents the treatment area configured for the dental CPT.

columns.name: paintTypeid
columns.description: This is a reference to the id column dentalpainttype table. It represents the paint type configured for the dental CPT.

columns.name: procedureCode
columns.description: This column stores the actual CPT code that corresponds to the itemid for the dental procedure.

columns.name: providerTime
columns.description: Dental appointments can be created by assigning different time slots for provider, resource and chair time (this is when the patient is on the chair and not necessarily required to have a provider/staff during this time). This column stores the details of the provider time slot in the form of a JSON string.

columns.name: resourceTime
columns.description: Dental appointments can be created by assigning different time slots for provider, resource and chair time (this is when the patient is on the chair and not necessarily required to have a provider/staff during this time). This column stores the details of the resource time slot in the form of a JSON string.

columns.name: chairTime
columns.description: Dental appointments can be created by assigning different time slots for provider, resource and chair time (this is when the patient is on the chair and not necessarily required to have a provider/staff during this time). This column stores the details of the chair time slot in the form of a JSON string.

columns.name: cptDuration
columns.description:
This column stores the default time duration for the dental CPT. The provider, time and chair slots will be split in this time duration. 
The column stores the time duration as an integer in minutes. Example - a value of 60 in this column means the procedure time is set to 60 minutes.

columns.name: aliasName
columns.description:
Every dental CPT can be given an alias name, which is stored in this column. When user adds that procedure to patient's appointment under "Planned procedures for today's visit", the alias name along with the certain other information will be shown on the Appointment slot.
The appointment slot has limited space on the UI, which is why the alias name is limited to 7 characters. It helps identify the type of procedure using a shortened notation.

table_description: This table stores any movements applied on the teeth for a patient. Each movement type for each tooth number will be stored as a separate row in the table.

columns.name: movementtype
columns.description: This column represents the type of movement being recorded in the row. Currently supported values are M, O, L, and MT for Mesial, Occlusal, Labial and Mesial Tip, respectively.

columns.name: value
columns.description: This column stores a numeric value representing the movement applied. It supports negative and positive integers.

table_description: This is the dictionary table of possible priorities that may be assigned to a dental procedure. The table is currently non-configurable and shipped with the entries.

columns.description: This column is set to 1 if the dentition is manually set by the user. If programmatically set (example - based on patient age), the value is 0.

columns.description: This is a text column that stores the drawing segments data for the dental tooth chart. It can contain a large amount of text data. Example: "M 10 10 L 20 20", "M 30 30 L 40 40", etc.

table_description: This table stores information about the status of dental treatment plans.

columns.description: This column stores the label for the dental treatment plan status, which can be used for display purposes. It is a variable character string with a maximum length of 20 characters and has a default value of an empty string. Example: 'PND', 'APR', 'CMP'.

table_description: This table stores information about files associated with different devices, such as their names, types, and related test IDs.

columns.name: FileName

table_description: This table stores information about various medical devices and their properties.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each device item. (Example: 1, 2, 3)

columns.name: Itemid
columns.description: identifier for the item, with a default value of 0. (Example: 101, 102, 103)

columns.name: ItemType
columns.description: Type of the device item, with possible values being 'Audio', 'Ecg', 'Holter', 'Oximetry', 'Scale', 'Spiro', 'Stress', 'MedicalImaging', 'Vision', and 'ABP'. (Example: 'Ecg', 'Holter', 'Oximetry')

columns.name: DeviceName
columns.description: Name of the device. (Example: 'CardioCheck', 'PulseOx', 'SpiroMeter')

columns.name: ModelNum
columns.description: Model number of the device. (Example: 'A123', 'B456', 'C789')

columns.name: VersionNum
columns.description: Version number of the device. (Example: '1.0', '2.0', '3.0')

columns.name: isReviewable
columns.description: Indicates if the device is reviewable, with 1 for yes and 0 for no. (Example: 1, 0)

columns.name: hasExtTestid
columns.description: Indicates if the device has an external test id, with 1 for yes and 0 for no. (Example: 1, 0)

columns.name: FaxReportType
columns.description: Type of the fax report, with possible values being 'JPG', 'PDF', 'SCP', 'DCM', 'BMP', 'GIF', 'PNG', 'DOC', and 'TIF'. Default value is 'PDF'. (Example: 'JPG', 'PDF', 'DOC')

columns.name: hasOrderTest
columns.description: Indicates if the device has an order test, with 1 for yes and 0 for no. Default value is 0. (Example: 1, 0)

columns.name: specialityformid
columns.description: identifier for the specialty form associated with the device. (Example: 1001, 1002, 1003)

columns.name: IsLegacyDevice
columns.description: Indicates if the device is a legacy device, with possible values being 'Yes' and 'no'. Default value is 'no'. (Example: 'Yes', 'no')

columns.name: Labid
columns.description: identifier for the lab associated with the device, with a default value of 0. (Example: 2001, 2002, 2003)

columns.name: isDiscreteData

columns.name: docTypeid

columns.name: docCatid
columns.description: identifier for the document category associated with the device, with a default value of 'XRay_doc'. (Example: 'XRay_doc', 'MRI_doc', 'CT_doc')

columns.name: docid
columns.description: identifier for the document associated with the device, with a default value of 3. (Example: 4001, 4002, 4003)

table_description: This table stores information about instances when a user breaks the glass to access a patient's document, including the user, patient, document, reason, accessing date, status, and IP address.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each break glass event. Example: 1, 2, 3

columns.name: userid
columns.description: identifier for the user who initiated the break glass event. Foreign key relation: `users` table, `UID` column. Example: 101, 102, 103

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: identifier for the patient whose document was accessed during the break glass event. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003

columns.name: documentid
columns.description: identifier for the document that was accessed during the break glass event. Foreign key relation: `document` table, `docid` column. Example: 2001, 2002, 2003

columns.name: reason
columns.description: Reason provided by the user for initiating the break glass event. Example: "Emergency access", "Patient consented"

columns.name: accessingdate
columns.description: Date and time when the break glass event occurred. Example: '2021-08-01 12:34:56'

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Status of the break glass event, such as "Active" or "Resolved". Example: "Active", "Resolved"

columns.name: ipAddress

table_description: This table stores information about the checklist selected from the I Quick-Launch button > Due Today popup for that encounter.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key and an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each row in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: ENCid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the id of the entity in another table. It is an integer value. Example: 10, 25, 42, etc. Foreign key relation: `otherTableName`.`id`

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: This is a variable character field with a maximum length of 50 characters, storing the name of the checklist item. It cannot be NULL and has a default value of an empty string. Example: "Task 1", "Task 2", "Task 3", etc.

columns.name: VALUE
columns.description: This is a tiny integer field that stores the value of the checklist item, indicating whether it is completed or not. It cannot be NULL and has a default value of 0. Example: 0 (not completed), 1 (completed).

table_description: This table stores the information about the checklist selected from the I Quick-Launch button > Due Today popup for the patient.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which uniquely identifies each record. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented as new records are added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: PATIENTid
columns.description: This column stores the unique identifier for each patient. It is an integer value and serves as a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `patients` table (not provided in the input). Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: This column stores the name of the task in the checklist. It is a variable character string with a maximum length of 50 characters. Example: 'Take medication', 'Check blood pressure', 'Schedule appointment', etc.

columns.name: VALUE
columns.description: This column stores the completion status of the task. It is a tiny integer value, where '0' indicates the task is not completed and '1' indicates the task is completed. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores information about ECG (Electrocardiogram) reports for patients, including file details, report dates, and review information.

columns.name: reportId
columns.description: This is an auto incremented primary key of This column .

columns.name: encId
columns.description: This column stores ID of an encounter for which ECG report information of Patient's visit is documented. This column refers column encounterId from enc table.

columns.name: patientId
columns.description: This column stores ID of Patient for whom information is documented. This column refers column pid from patients table.

columns.name: labId
columns.description: This column stores id of the lab which has ECG reports associated with it. This column refers column reportId from labdata table.

columns.name: labType
columns.description: This column stores values 0 / 1 / 3 to indicate what type of order is placed. 0 - if a Lab is ordered , 1 - if a Diagnostic Imaging is ordered, 3 - if a Procedure is ordered.

columns.name: filePath
columns.description: This column stores report local file path.

columns.name: fileName1
columns.description: This column stores File name for Pre ECG report.

columns.name: fileName2
columns.description: Name of the second ECG report file, if applicable. (e.g., "ecg_report_2.pdf")

columns.name: reportDate
columns.description: Date when the ECG report was generated. (e.g., "2021-10-01")

columns.name: reviewDate
columns.description: Date when the ECG report was reviewed by a medical professional, if applicable. (e.g., "2021-10-02")

columns.name: reviewedBy
columns.description: Name of the medical professional who reviewed the ECG report. (e.g., "Dr. John Doe")

columns.name: technician
columns.description: Name of the technician who performed the ECG. (e.g., "Jane Smith")

columns.name: delFlag
columns.description: Integer indicating whether the ECG report has been deleted (1) or not (0). (e.g., 0)

columns.name: FaxReportFileName1
columns.description: This column stores Fax File name for Pre ECG report.

columns.name: FaxReportFileName2
columns.description: This column stores Fax File name for Post ECG report.

columns.name: comments
columns.description: Text containing any additional comments or notes about the ECG report. (e.g., "Patient experienced mild chest pain during the test.")

columns.name: ftpdirpath
columns.description: File path where the ECG report is stored on the FTP server, if applicable. (e.g., "/ftp/ecg_reports/patient_1001/")

columns.name: pdfuploadsuccess
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 indicating FTP file upload status. 0 - Fail , 1 - Success.

columns.name: sdkversion
columns.description: This column stores information about sdk version when performing test.

table_description: This table stores information about insurance and driver's license documents uploaded by users during the e-check-in process.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: uid
columns.description: User identifier, referring to the user who uploaded the document. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: insuranceid
columns.description: Insurance identifier, referring to the specific insurance record associated with the document. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: filename
columns.description: Name of the file uploaded by the user. Example: "insurance_card.jpg", "driver_license.png".

columns.name: delflag
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the record has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: ts_utc
columns.description: time stamp in UTC when the record was created or updated. Example: "2021-09-01 12:34:56".

columns.name: cardview
columns.description: A short description or label for the uploaded document. Example: "Front side", "Back side".

columns.name: imageguid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the image file stored in the system. Example: "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-g7h8-i9j0-k1l2m3n4o5p6".

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: Identifier for the specific encounter or appointment associated with the document. Example: "E123", "E124", "E125".

columns.name: apuid
columns.description: Identifier for the application user who uploaded the document. Example: "APU101", "APU102", "APU103".

columns.name: websync
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the record has been synchronized with the web application (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Status of the document, represented by a small integer. Example: 0 (Pending), 1 (Approved), 2 (Rejected).

columns.name: TYPE
columns.description: Type of the document, either 'insurance' or 'driverlicense'. Example: "insurance", "driverlicense".

table_description: This table stores medical data related to a patient's electronic check-in, including surgery history, hospitalization history, medication list, and an allergy list.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the echeckinmedicaldata table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: uid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the user (patient) associated with the medical data. Foreign key relation: `users` table, `uid` column. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: encid
columns.description: Unique identifier for the encounter associated with the medical data. Foreign key relation: `enc` table, `encounterID` column. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: surglist
columns.description: A string containing the patient's surgery history, with each surgery separated by a delimiter. Example: "Appendectomy;Gallbladder removal".

columns.name: hosplist
columns.description: A string containing the patient's hospitalization history, with each hospitalization separated by a delimiter. Example: "St. Mary's Hospital;General Hospital".

columns.name: medlist
columns.description: A string containing the patient's medication list, with each medication separated by a delimiter. Example: "Aspirin;Lisinopril;Metformin".

columns.name: allergylist
columns.description: A string containing the patient's allergy list, with each allergy separated by a delimiter. Example: "Penicillin;Peanuts;Shellfish".

columns.name: delflag
columns.description: A tiny integer indicating whether the record has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: modifieddate
columns.description: A datetime value indicating the last time the record was modified. Example: '2022-01-01 12:34:56'.

table_description: This table stores categoryId based on caret template log Id .

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT. This column stores integer value which grows with every category is copy or merged through carets. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index

columns.name: logid
columns.description: This column stores the integer value of the log id associated with a specific caret category. It has a foreign key relation with the `ecri_template_cp_logs` table, specifically the `id` column. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: categoryid
columns.description: It stores category id of category which is copied or merged through carets. It refers to itemid column of items table.

table_description: This table stores notes which is merged using carets and which does not have category id.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT. This column stores integer value which grows with every text note is copy or merged through carets. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index

columns.name: logid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `ecri_template_cp_logs` table. It establishes a relationship between the `ecri_caret_logs` and `ecri_template_cp_logs` tables. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: It stores notes (does not belongs to item or category) which is copied or merged through carets. It refers to itemid column of items table.

table_description: This table stores sources of the clinical notes copied, pasted or merged to an encounter.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, containing unique integer values to identify each qualifier in the table. Example values: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: source
columns.description: This column contains the source of the qualifier as a varchar (up to 300 characters). Example values: "Patient-Specific Template", "Clipboard", etc.

table_description: This table stores logs of clinical notes copied or merged into a set of Progress Notes from either a template or caret encounters.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT. This column stores integer value which could grow with every copy or merge activity of each section in Progress Note. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY index

columns.name: module
columns.description: The name of the module where the copy or merge operation was performed in Pt. Specific template or carets, stored as a varchar. For example: "PN", etc.

columns.name: featureid
columns.description: It stores source of copy/merge. It refers to id column in table ecri_cp_qualifiers.

columns.name: copyMergeFlag
columns.description: A tinyint flag indicating whether the operation was a copy (1) or a merge (0). For example: 0 or 1.

columns.name: srcid
columns.description: It stores source encounter id. This column has a foreign key relation with the `enc` table's `encounterid` column.

columns.name: destid
columns.description: It stores destination encounter id. This column has a foreign key relation with the `enc` table's `encounterid` column.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: The identifier of the user who performed the copy or merge operation, with integer values. This column has a foreign key relation with the `users` table's `UID` column. For example: 501, 502, 503, etc.

columns.name: entrydatetime
columns.description: It stores date and time when notes are copy/merged through Pt. Specific Template or carets.

table_description: This table stores information about print logs for EHR (Electronic Health Records), including details about the print job, user, and patient.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each print log entry. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: parameters
columns.description: Text containing the parameters used for the print job. Example: copies: 2, orientation: portrait.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Type of print job, such as the document being printed. Example: prescription, lab_report, invoice.

columns.name: macaddress
columns.description: MAC address of the device that initiated the print job. Example: 00:1A:79:12:34:56.

columns.name: datecreated
columns.description: Date and time when the print log entry was created. Example: 2021-09-01 12:34:56.

columns.name: dateupdated
columns.description: Date and time when the print log entry was last updated. Example: 2021-09-02 14:23:12.

columns.name: isprinted
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the print job was successful (1) or not (0). Example: 0 or 1.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: Identifier for the user who initiated the print job. This could be a foreign key referring to the id column in a user table. Example: 42.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: Identifier for the patient encounter associated with the print job. This could be a foreign key referring to the id column in an encounters table. Example: 123.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: Identifier for the patient associated with the print job. This could be a foreign key referring to the id column in a patients table. Example: 789.

columns.name: content
columns.description:
Long text containing the content of the document being printed. Example: Patient Name: John Doe
DOB: 01/01/1980
Prescription: Amoxicillin 500mg
.

columns.name: statusMsg
columns.description: Status message for the print job, indicating success or failure. Example: Printed successfully or Printer error: out of paper.

columns.name: isSF_Cat

columns.name: map_specialityid

Table stores community mapping of HPI and Examination properties and  Social History, Physical Examination, Preventive Medicine line items.
 
id is auto increment and primary key of the table.

table_description: This tables stores options to structured questions stored in the ecwstructitems table.

columns.name: ecwOptionid

table_description: This table stores information about claim status category codes in the EDI 277CA (Claim Acknowledgement) transaction set.

columns.name: categoryorder
columns.description: An integer value representing the order in which the claim status categories should be displayed or processed. Example: 0, 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: A tiny integer value (0 or 1) indicating whether the record has been deleted or not. A value of 0 means the record is active, while a value of 1 means the record has been deleted. Example: 0 (active), 1 (deleted).

table_description: This tables store CPT Form Question Information which is included ANSI Professional Claim in Loop 2440

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, containing a unique integer value for each question in the table. It is automatically incremented as new questions are added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: AssignedId
columns.description: This column contains a varchar value (up to 20 characters) that represents an assigned identifier for the question. It can be NULL if no identifier is assigned. Example: "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", etc.

columns.name: Question
columns.description: This column contains a longtext value that represents the text of the question. Example: "What is your name?", "What is your age?", etc.

columns.name: Questiontype
columns.description: This column contains a tinyint value (3 digits) that represents the type of question. It has a default value of '0'. Example: 1(Yes/No Response), 2 (Text/Uncodified response), 3 (Date), 4 (Percentage).

columns.name: forms_id
columns.description: This column contains an integer value that represents the ID of the form the question belongs to. It has a default value of '0'. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `edi_forms` table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This column contains a tinyint value (1 digit) that indicates whether the question has been deleted or not. It has a default value of '0'. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

This column stores value 0/1. 0 - not in used , 1 - Services performed by a nurse practitioner 'Incident To' a physician.  If it is 'Incident To' claim, Supervising physician provider number will be put in box 24K.

table_description: This table stores the summary of encounters and their corresponding eICR transaction logs.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column that uniquely identifies each record in the `eicr_encounter_summary` table. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits and is auto-incremented. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: This column stores the encounter ID associated with the summary. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits. This column has a foreign key relation with the `enc` table's `encounterid` column. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: eicr_transaction_log_id
columns.description: This column stores the EICR transaction log ID associated with the encounter summary. It is an integer with a maximum length of 11 digits. This column has a foreign key relation with the `eicr_transaction_logs` table's `id` column. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003, etc.

table_description: This table stores information about error reasons related to eICR (Electronic Initial Case Report) transactions.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is an integer column that serves as the primary key and uniquely identifies each error reason. It is an auto-incrementing value. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: This is a varchar(255) column that stores the human-readable name or description of the error reason.

table_description: This table stores the Electronic Case Reporting transaction logs for electronic health record (EHR) encounters, including information about the user, transaction type, status, and other related details.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each transaction log entry. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: Identifier for the encounter associated with the transaction log. Foreign key relation to `enc` table's `encounterID` column. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: Identifier for the user who performed the transaction. Foreign key relation to `users` table's `uid` column. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: transaction_type
columns.description: Numeric code representing the type of transaction. Example: 1 (Outgoing), 2 (Incoming)

columns.name: transaction_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the transaction, represented as a string. Example: "TX123", "TX124", "TX125".

columns.name: priority
columns.description: Numeric code representing the priority level of the transaction.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Numeric code representing the status of the transaction.

columns.name: error_reason
columns.description: Numeric code representing the reason for a transaction failure, if applicable.

columns.name: transaction_time
columns.description: time stamp of when the transaction occurred. Example: "2021-09-01 12:34:56", "2021-09-02 14:23:45".

columns.name: isResent
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the transaction has been resent (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: SUBJECT
columns.description: Subject of the transaction, represented as a string.

columns.name: summary_preview_text
columns.description: Preview text of the transaction summary, represented as a string.

columns.name: transmission_mode
columns.description: Numeric code representing the mode of transmission for the transaction. Example: 1 (Automatic),2 (Manual).

columns.description: This column represents the patient id for which consent has been saved. It refers to the user.UID column.

columns.name: ecwmpi
columns.description: This column represent eEHX enabled patient's ecwmpi id. This is gUID value.

columns.name: timestamp
columns.description: This column represents when an entry was made into this column. It is a time stamp column that defaults to the current date and time.

columns.name: EnableEmpi
columns.description: This column contains the enable empi value, which has a value of 1 only if the patient has opted-in with EHX, otherwise it will be 0.

columns.name: eCROptInOption
columns.description: This column contains the value of patient consent option with eEHX. Possible values include: 'OptOut', 'OptInThisFac', 'OptInAllFac,' and 'OptInThisFac'.

columns.name: ReceivedConsent
columns.description: This column contains the value of patient consent to eEHX. A value of '1' means the patient has consented to eEHX, and a value of '0' means the patient not consented to eEHX.

columns.name: DateSigned
columns.description: This column contains the date when a patient signed the consent form. Example: "2021-07-01"

columns.name: MatchFound
columns.description: This is a dead column, not used in the system, and the system does not populate this column.

columns.name: delFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint (1) field that indicates whether the login record has been deleted or not. A value of '0' means the record is not deleted, and a value of '1' means the record is deleted. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an integer value, and it cannot be NULL. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Facid
columns.description: This is a dead column, not used from the system, and the system does not populate this column value.

columns.name: optinpracticecode
columns.description: This column represents a patient's practice code.

columns.name: OptinFacilityid
columns.description: This column represents a patient's optin facility id. It refers to the edi_facilities.id column.

columns.name: OptinFacilityName
columns.description: This column represents a patient's optin facility name. It refers to the edi_facilities.name column.

columns.name: FacGroupid
columns.description: This column is a dead column. It had been used with the MultiMaster eEHX setup, but that is no longer supported by the system.

columns.name: ConsentSignedByGuarantor
columns.description: This is a dead column. It is not used by the system, and the system doesn't populate the column value.

columns.name: IsBeneficiary
columns.description: A flag indicating if the patient is a beneficiary (integer, 0 or 1). Example: 1
