table_description: This table stores details of milestones related to specific encounters, including their outcomes, triggers, statuses, and interventions.

columns.name: MileStoneDetailid
columns.description: The unique identifier for each milestone detail entry. (Examples include: 1, 2, 3).

columns.name: MileStoneid
columns.description: identifier for the milestone associated with the encounter. (Foreign key relation: `milestone.milestoneid`) (Example: 101, 102, 103)

columns.name: Encounterid
columns.description: identifier for the encounter associated with the milestone. (Foreign key relation: `enc.encounterid`) (Example: 1001, 1002, 1003)

columns.name: Outcome
columns.description: The description of the outcome of the milestone. (Examples include: 'Successful', 'Failed', 'In Progress').

columns.name: MileStoneTrigger
columns.description: A single character representing the trigger for the milestone. (Examples include: 'A', 'B', 'C').

columns.name: ActiveDate
columns.description: The date when the milestone became active. (Examples include: '2022-01-01', '2022-01-15', '2022-02-01').

columns.name: Category
columns.description: The category of the milestone (e.g.,'Health', 'Education', 'Social').

columns.name: Status
columns.description: The integer representing the status of the milestone with '0' for inactive and '1' for active).

columns.name: TargetScore1
columns.description: The first target score for the milestone (e.g., 0, 1, 2).

columns.name: TargetScore2
columns.description: The second target score for the milestone (e.g., 0, 10, 20).

columns.name: CurrentScore
columns.description: The current score of the milestone (e.g., 0, 5, 15).

columns.name: Intervention1
columns.description: The description of the first intervention related to the milestone. (Examples include: 'Counseling', 'Medication', 'Support Group', etc.).

columns.name: Intervention2
columns.description: The description of the second intervention related to the milestone. (Examples include: 'Counseling', 'Medication', 'Support Group', etc.).

columns.name: TargetDate
columns.description: The target date for achieving the milestone. (Examples include: '2022-03-01', '2022-03-15', '2022-04-01', etc.).

columns.name: ResolvedDate
columns.description: The date when the milestone was resolved. (Examples include: '2022-03-01', '2022-03-15', '2022-04-01', etc.).

columns.name: Detail
columns.description: Additional text details about the milestone. (Examples include: 'Patient showed improvement after intervention', 'Milestone not achieved due to lack of resources', etc.).

table_description: This table stores structured data related to mobile encounters, including notes, transcription information, and user details.

columns.name: id
columns.description: A text column that stores the data associated with the synchronization action. This could be the data being inserted, updated, or deleted, depending on the action type.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: A varchar(500) column that stores the SQL WHERE clause used to filter the records affected by the synchronization action. This column is optional and can be empty if no filtering is needed. Example: "user_id = 5 AND status = 'active'".

columns.name: notes
columns.description: A datetime column that stores the time stamp when the synchronization action was created. This column is optional and can be NULL if the creation time is not needed. Example: '2021-09-15 12:34:56'.

columns.name: transcriptionid
columns.description: A smallint(6) column that indicates whether the synchronization action has been performed on the web server or not. It has a default value of '0'. Example: 0 (not synced), 1 (synced).

columns.name: userid
columns.description: A tinyint(2) column that stores the number of times the synchronization action has failed. It has a default value of '0'. Example: 0, 1, 2, etc.

columns.name: visittype
columns.description: This is an integer column that represents the unique identifier of the P2P (Peer-to-Peer) Network Provider Interface for the recipient. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: scribedstatus
columns.description: This is a varchar(700) column that stores the name of the P2P provider for the recipient. Example: 'ProviderA', 'ProviderB', 'ProviderC'.

columns.name: searchKey
columns.description: Unique identifier for each multisatisfiedalert record. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: created
columns.description: A datetime value indicating when the mobile structured data record was created. It can be NULL. Example: '2021-08-01 12:34:56', '2021-08-02 14:30:00'.

table_description: This table stores information about referrals requests received  from P2P. Includes healthcare referring and receiving providers details, procedures,diagnosis and   has column to store referral xml which contains patient details name, address, date of birth.

columns.name: Reqid
columns.description: This is auto-incremented primary key in This column . This column represents unique requests received over P2P.

columns.name: refFrom
columns.description: This column stores id of the provider from whom referral has been received. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: authNo
columns.description: This column refers to free text string entered into Auth Code filled in the user interface. This code represents Auth Code provided by insurance company for the referral. Authorization Types and codes are created by end user.

columns.name: authtype
columns.description: This column stores value of field Auth Type (Authorization Type) selected by end user on the user interface. Authorization Types and codes are created by end user.

columns.name: date
columns.description: This column stores date on which the referral was created for the patient. Date is stored in 'YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.000' format.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: This column stores reason why the referral was created. Reason could be free text or pre-configured keywords selected by the provider/staff.

columns.name: diagnosis
columns.description: This column stores patient's diagnosis for which referral as created. Column has been declared as TEXT because column stores ICD code with the text for diagnosis and may store more than one diagnosis separated by "|". i.e 721.3 - Lumbosacral spondylosis without myelopathy|333.94 - Restless legs syndrome RLS|311 - Depressive disorder, not elsewhere classified|

columns.name: refStDate
columns.description: This column stores start date of the referral after which referral can be used by the patient for the visit and the date is selected by provider/staff.

columns.name: refEnddate
columns.description: This column stores end date of the referral after which referral can not be used by the patient  and the date is selected by provider/staff.

columns.name: visitsAllowed
columns.description: This column stores a number, which represents number of times visit to referred provider will be allowed with the referral.

columns.name: visitsUsed
columns.description: This column stores a number, which represents the number of visits to the referred provider patient has used with the referral.

columns.name: RefTo
columns.description: This column stores an id of a provider under To section in User Interface. Provider is to whom patient has been referred to. This column refer to UID column in user table.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: This column stores free text notes documented by provider/staff under General Notes section under Notes tab in the User Interface.

columns.name: referralType
columns.description: This column stores a character I/O to indicate type of the referral being stored. I - Incoming Referral, O - Outgoing Referral, PTRECORD_I - Incoming Patient Record, PTRECORD_O - Outgoing Patient Record.

columns.name: priority
columns.description: This column stores priority of the referral documented by provider/staff. 0 - Routine, 1 - Urgent, 2 - Stat

columns.name: assignedTo
columns.description: This column stores name of the provider/staff to whom this referral has been assigned to.

columns.name: assignedToid
columns.description: This column stores id of a provider/staff to whom the referral has been assigned to in the user interfaceby end user. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores a digit to indicate current status of the referral received over P2P network. 0 - Referral is Open, 1 - Consultation is pending, 2 - Referral is addressed.

columns.name: fromfacility
columns.description: This column stores id of a facility selected by the end user under From section in user interfacewhile creating the referral. This column refers to id column in edi_facilities table.

columns.name: ToFacility
columns.description: This column stores id of a facility selected by the end user under To section in user interfacewhile creating the referral. This column refers to id column in edi_facilities table.

columns.name: speciality
columns.description: This column stores id for a specialty of the practice for which the referral has been created. This column refers to id column in edi_speciality column.

columns.name: ReferralNumber
columns.description: This column stores Referral Number provided by a payer for prior authorization of a referral. If Referral Number is missing and if insurance 'requires referral' then claim can not be generated.

columns.name: clinicalNotes
columns.description: This column stores free text notes documented by provider/staff under Clinical Notes section under Notes tab in the User Interface.

columns.name: refEncid
columns.description: This column stores id of the encounter from which outgoing referral has been created. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: extRefid
columns.description: This column stores id of a referral from practice which sent referral.

columns.name: apptdate
columns.description: This column stores date for an appointment of a patient with referred provider.

columns.name: ReceivedDate
columns.description: This column stores date from the Received Date field in the User Interface. Date when referral was received.

columns.name: procedures
columns.description: This column stores an ids and names of procedures selected by provider/staff in the user interfacewhile creating the referral. Datatype TEXT was selected because provider/staff may select more than one procedures which are separated by "|" while being stored in this column. i.e 11750 - Excision Ingrown Nail|11730 - AVULSION PLATE PART/COMPLT SIM|11721 - Debridement nails 6+|11720 - Debridement nails 1-5|11719 - Nail Trim any number|

table_description: This table stores the entries of saved and updated worksheets.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores the encounter id of the worksheet encounter.

columns.name: worksheetid
columns.description:
This column stores the id of the worksheet. 
The worksheetid column corresponds to the id column in the nt_worksheet_list table.

columns.name: islocked
columns.description:
This column hold the value of the locked status of the worksheet.
If islocked = 1, then the worksheet is locked
If islocked  = 0, then the worksheet is unlocked.

columns.name: data
columns.description:
This column stores the data that is filled in the worksheet in an xml format.
As part of data-validation, the xml tags are encrypted while saving the data. 
It is decrypted when the data is loaded.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the record is deleted or not. 1 means deleted, and 0 means not deleted. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: created_date
columns.description: The date and time when the record was created. Example: '2021-09-01 12:34:56'.

columns.name: modified_date
columns.description: The date and time when the record was last modified. Example: '2021-09-02 14:56:32'.

columns.name: print_data
columns.description:
This column stores the entire worksheet data in an xml format. 
The data from this column is fetched while printing / faxing.

columns.name: sf_data
columns.description: This column stores the structured data details in the XML tags format.

columns.name: modified_by
columns.description: This column stores the user id of the logged in provider.

columns.name: print_dataNo_JS
columns.description: This column stores the entire worksheet data in an xml format without the Javascript code.

columns.name: PRINT_PDF_DATA
columns.description:
This column stores the entire worksheet data in an xml format. 
The data from this column is fetched when the PDF format for the worksheet is enabled.

table_description: This table stores information about worksheets, their names, URLs, and other related properties.

columns.name: id
columns.description:
The id column is the primary key
It is unique for each worksheets.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description:
The name column stores the name of the worksheet with respect to the id column. 
Datatype is varchar

columns.name: form_url
columns.description:
The form_url coulmn stores the name of the jsp of the respective worksheet.
Datatype is text

columns.name: isWorksheet
columns.description:
The isWorksheet column denotes the worksheet deployed on the server.
isWorksheet is equal to 1 if the worksheet is deployed and present.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description:
The deleteflag column stores the value as 1 / 0 for worksheets.
deleteflag  = 1 : The worksheet wont show up in the worksheet list
deleteflag  = 0 : The worksheet would show up in the worksheet list

columns.name: docttype
columns.description:
The doctype column stores the doctype value of the worksheets.
Its not in use. Holds NULL value.

columns.name: displayindex
columns.description: The displayindex column stores the display index with respect to worksheets

columns.name: linkedids
columns.description: The linkedids columns store the linked ids of the worksheet.

columns.name: default_name
columns.description: The default_name column stores the default name of the worksheets.

table_description: This table stores follow-up appointment details for the Open Access feature.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores id of an encounter for which followup appointment was created. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: followupdate
columns.description: This column stores date of a future appointment created for followup. Date is stored in 'YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.000' format.

columns.name: Patientid
columns.description: This column stores id of a patient for whom followup appointment was created. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: doctorid
columns.description: This column stores id of a provider with whom followup appointment has been scheduled. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: date
columns.description: This column stores date of a current appointment whose encounterid is mentioned in corresponding encounterid column. Date is stored in 'YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.000' format.

columns.name: facilityid
columns.description: This column stores id of a facility where encounter mentioned in corresponding encounterid column in This column  took place. This column refers to id column in edi_facility table.

table_description: This table stores information about encounters created through healow, including healow id,their payment status and the time they were last updated.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is auto-incremented primary key in This column .

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores an encounter id when appointments are created from healow through openaccess. This value refers to the encounterid column of the enc table.

columns.name: healow_uid
columns.description: This column stores the Healow unique identifier of a patient who is enrolled for Open Access Campaign. This is an int(11) type. And the default value is 0. The actual value is sent from healow and there are no other references of this value in the EMR DB

columns.name: payment_status
columns.description: This is an enumeration column that stores the payment status of the encounter. It can have one of the following values: 'N/A', 'Pending', 'Success', or 'Failed'.

columns.name: updated_ts_utc
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the time stamp of when the encounter payment status was last updated in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Example: '2022-01-01 12:34:56'

table_description: This table stores information related to ocular encounters, including the verification of ocular history and ocular surgical history, as well as the users who verified these histories.

table_description: This table stores information about ocular surgical history for each encounter.

columns.name: encounterid

columns.description: This is used to store the date related to the reason being recorded. This date column may contain two or more concatenated dates  eg - '10/14 & 12/13'. This column is not used in 'where' clause. Date may not present for all the reasons hence NULLable and default value is an empty string.

columns.name: displayIndex
columns.description: Determines the order in which the reasons will be displayed on the Progress Notes and Ocular Surgical History window. In case no display order is not present, a default of 1 is stored.

columns.name: DaysLeftAdjustNumber

---This column is of DATE type in MySQL schema.--

Contains auto incremented id, datatype is INT. This column stores integer value which could grow with number of transactions added and�hence integer is selected

. It is AUTO_INCREMENT column and has PRIMARY KEY constraint defined on this column

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This column stores unique id of a Patient which references the UID column of the user table. The data type chosen is INT. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL.

columns.description: Contains enrollmentid value referenced from id column of the�rpm_enrollment_details table, datatype is INT. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL..

columns.name: reading_date
columns.description: Reading date is the datetime for which we are receiving the data for any of the devices.�This column stores date hence Date is selected. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL. By default�'1901-01-01'/�'0000-00-00' for MSSQL/MYSQL accordingly�is chosen.

columns.name: review_status
columns.description: This column is introduced to maintain if the review for all devices for a patient is completed on a daily basis. It contains review status with values 0 and 1,(0-Pending,1-Complete). The datatype is TININT. By default we maintain a value as Pending. But once the review is complete for all devices we maintain it as 1.This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL.

columns.name: data_status
columns.description: This column is introduced to maintain if any one of the devices has either data not received/Contains data status of reading for all devices for a daily basis. If anyone of the device has below criteria, the corresponding value is maintained in this column. This uses TINYINT-- 0 - data_not_received, 1 - abnormal,2 abnormal/data_not_received, 3 complete.By default we would maintain 0 which means the data is not received. We have kept the data type of this field TINYINT as currently there are 4 possible values - 0, 1, 2 and 3.

columns.name: isNonbillableDevice
columns.description: This column is introduced to check if any one of the devices for a patient has readings coming from a non prescribed vendor which could make it ineligible for billing. The data type chosen is TINYINT.This column could potentially contains contains two value 0 and 1. If anyone of the device has a reading that is non prescribed/non billable then we would maintain a value 1,else 0. By default we would maintain 0 and as it always has a value we defined it as NOT NULL

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: Flag indicates the last reading received for a day is deleted, datatype is tinyint - 0 - Not Deleted, 1 - Deleted. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL. By default, this column should not be in Deleted status hence default 0 is chosen.

columns.name: modifiedDatetime
columns.description: Contains "modifiedDatetime " value when a user is adds/updates reading for any of the devices and datatype is DATETIME. By default, current system datetime needs to be inserted. This field will always have a value hence defined as NOT NULL

columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and is an integer that uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an auto-incrementing value, meaning it will automatically increase by 1 for each new record added to the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: RAF_Patientid
columns.description: The unique identifier for the patient associated with the RAF score. This refers to the `Patientid` column in a `patients` table. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: RAF_Score
columns.description: The RAF score for the patient, which is a float value. Example: 1.2, 2.5, 3.1, etc.

columns.name: RAF_Year
columns.description: The year for which the RAF score is applicable, stored as a datetime value. Example: '2022-01-01 00:00:00', '2023-01-01 00:00:00', '2024-01-01 00:00:00', etc.

columns.name: RAF_LastUpdated
columns.description: The time stamp when the RAF score was last updated, stored as a datetime value. Example: '2022-07-15 14:30:00', '2022-08-10 10:45:00', '2022-09-01 16:00:00', etc.

columns.name: RAF_DeleteFlag
columns.description: A tinyint value indicating whether the RAF score entry has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores the relationship between patients and their registry groups.

table_description: This table stores information about the sexual orientation of patients, including the reason for the orientation, the person who modified the information, and the status of the record.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.description: Indicates whether the record is active (1) or inactive (0). Example: 1, 0.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: Indicates whether the record has been deleted (1) or not (0). Example: 1, 0.

columns.name: added_on
columns.description: The date and time when the record was added to the table. Example: '2021-09-01 12:34:56'.

columns.name: inactive_date

columns.name: modality

table_description: This table stores information about the residential details of patients in a healthcare facility.

columns.name: PatientId
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and represents a unique identifier for each patient. It is an integer value and cannot be NULL. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: FacilityId
columns.description: This column represents the identifier of the healthcare facility where the patient is staying. It is an integer value and can be NULL if the patient is not currently in a facility. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: Room
columns.description: This column stores the room number or name where the patient is staying within the facility. It is a varchar(20) and can be NULL if the patient is not currently in a room. Example: 'A101', 'B203', 'C305', etc.

columns.name: Bed
columns.description: This column stores the bed number or name assigned to the patient within the room. It is a varchar(100) and can be NULL if the patient is not currently assigned a bed. Example: 'Bed 1', 'Bed 2', 'Bed 3', etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column is a tinyint(4) and indicates whether the record has been deleted or not. A value of '0' means the record is active, while a value of '1' means the record has been deleted. Example: 0, 1.

This column stores one of the below values as the type of the problem:
Finding of Functional Performance Activity, Cognitive Function Finding, and Complaint.

table_description: This is the child table for every procedure documented for patients. Any procedure documented for a patient may have one or more entries in this table. It stores a history of changes made to the procedure over time since many dental procedures are not completed in a single encounter and progress over weeks/months. Each change to the procedure will have a new row in the table, and they all share the same ProcNum. This table has a many-to-one relationship with procedurelog.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the auto-increment primary key column for the table.

columns.name: ProcNum
columns.description: This is a reference to the column ProcNum of the table procedurelog. This column  has a many-to-one relationship with procedurelog, with entries created for each change to the procedure. This maintains a history of the changes made to the procedure.

columns.name: ProcDate
columns.description: This column stores the procedure date, which is usually the date the procedure was first documented, or the date of the encounter where the procedure was first documented.

columns.name: procfee
columns.description: This column stores the fee associated to the procedure.

columns.name: Surf
columns.description: This column stores the surfaces (if applicable) for which the procedure is applied. It's a combination of all applicable surfaces stored as a single string (example - MOD, DL, MODBL, etc).

columns.name: ToothNum
columns.description: This column stores the tooth number (if applicable) for which the procedure is applied.

columns.name: ToothRange
columns.description: If the procedure applied is for multiple teeth, or a specific treatment area, such as quadrant, arch, sextant, or full mouth, that information is stored in this column.

columns.name: Priority
columns.description: This column represents the priority of the procedure and is a reference to the column priorityNo of table dentalpriority.

columns.name: ProcStatus
columns.description: This column references the id column of dentalentrystatus table and identifies the entry status of the procedure.

columns.name: ProvNum
columns.description: This column references the UID column of user table and identifies the provider id associated to the procedure.

columns.description: This column stores the completed date of the procedure.

columns.description: This column references the itemid column of items table and identifies the CPT code associated to the procedure.

columns.name: ModifiedByTrUserid
columns.description: This column references the UID column of user table and identifies the id of the user who modified the procedure last.

columns.name: DateModified
columns.description: This column stores the time stamp of when the procedure was last modified.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This column, when set to 1, soft deletes the procedure entry. By default, when 0, the procedure is not flagged as deleted.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column references the encounterid column of en table and identifies the encounter id where the instance of this procedure entry was added/updated. For procedures added from the Patient Hub, this column stores -1.

columns.name: procnote
columns.description: This column stores the text that was documented as notes for the procedure.

columns.name: migrationFlag
columns.description: This column indicates if the procedure was documented in eCW database through the regular use of the product, or if it was migrated from a different system to eCW database. Value is set to a non-zero value for migrated procedures.

columns.name: PriorAuthStatus
columns.description:
This column stores the prior authorization status for the procedure. A prior authorization provides advance approval for the planned service, which is generally valid for a fixed period of time. 

The allowed values in this column are 1 (not approved), 2 (requires approval), 3 (approved), and 0 which is the default value (no prior authorization status associated).

columns.name: SelfPay
columns.description: This column is set to 1 when the patient opts to self-pay for a procedure. By default, the column is set to 0 which is the case when self-pay is not set.

columns.name: PriorAuthNum
columns.description: This column stores the prior authorization number obtained from the insurance company when the prior authorization has been approved for a procedure.

columns.name: PriorAuthExpiryDate
columns.description: This is the column that stores the expiry date for a prior authorization. As mentioned previously, each prior authorization is valid for a fixed period from when it is issued (typically 60 days).

columns.name: dx2
columns.description: This column references the itemid column of items table and identifies one of up to four ICDs associated to the procedure.

columns.name: dx3
columns.description: This column references the itemid column of items table and identifies one of up to four ICDs associated to the procedure.

columns.name: dx4
columns.description: This column references the itemid column of items table and identifies one of up to four ICDs associated to the procedure.

columns.name: smartnotenum
columns.description: This column references the primary key column of 'smartnote' table and identifies whether a default smart note was applied to the procedure through favorite button configuration.

columns.name: ptPortion
columns.description: This column stores the patient estimate calculated for a procedure based on fee schedule and insurance.

columns.name: allowedFee
columns.description: This column stores the allowed Fee amount of the procedure based on insurance and Fee schedule.

columns.name: feeUpdated
columns.description: This column stores value 0 or 1 to indicate whether patient estimate is calculated for the patient or not . By default the value is 0, which means patient estimate is not calculated yet. The column value changes to 1, when Treatment plan is accessed for the patient and fees gets calculated for the procedure.

columns.name: feesUpdatedDate
columns.description: This column stores the time stamp of when the procedure fees was last calculated.

columns.name: resourceid
columns.description: This column references the UID column of user table and identifies the id of the Resource associated to the procedure.

columns.description: This column stores the insurance id of the patient's Dental insurance used for calculation of Treatment plan estimates, at a procedure level. This refers to "insid" column of "insurance" table.

columns.description: This column stores the Fee schedule id of the patient used for calculation of Treatment plan estimates, at a procedure level. This refers to "id" column of "feeschlist" table.

columns.description: This column stores the insurance estimate calculated for a patient based on insurance coverage percentage set for each procedure. This value depends on the dental insurance and fee schedule assigned to the patient.

columns.name: insCoveragePerc
columns.description: This column stores the insurance coverage percentage set for a procedure. Insurance coverage percentage for a procedure, under that insurance can be set either on Insurance CPT mapping screen or Dental Plans screen.

columns.description: This column stores surfaces for which Class V fillings were applied. It is necessary to store this information to display on the UI the set of surfaces which have class V fillings and the set of surfaces which do not.

table_description: This table stores information about patient orders, including order details, status, and scheduling.

columns.name: orderid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each order (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: Identifier for the patient encounter associated with the order (e.g., 100, 101, 102).

columns.name: userid
columns.description: Identifier for the user who created the order (e.g., 10, 11, 12).

columns.name: orderedByid
columns.description: Identifier for the user who authorized the order (e.g., 20, 21, 22).

columns.name: orderItemid
columns.description: Identifier for the specific item being ordered (e.g., 1000, 1001, 1002).

columns.name: orderDateTime
columns.description: Date and time when the order was created (e.g., 2021-08-01 14:30:00).

columns.name: startDateTime
columns.description: Date and time when the order should start (e.g., 2021-08-01 15:00:00).

columns.name: endDateTime
columns.description: Date and time when the order should end (e.g., 2021-08-01 16:00:00).

columns.name: isRecurringOrder
columns.description: Indicates if the order is recurring (1) or not (0) (e.g., 0, 1).

columns.name: orderStatus
columns.description: Numeric code representing the status of the order (e.g., 0, 1, 2).

columns.name: orderFrequencyid
columns.description: Identifier for the frequency of the order (e.g., 30, 31, 32).

columns.name: orderPriority
columns.description: Indicates the priority of the order, with 1 being high priority and 0 being normal priority (e.g., 0, 1).

columns.name: orderNotes
columns.description: Additional notes about the order (e.g., Patient requires extra monitoring).

columns.name: orderInstructions
columns.description: Specific instructions for the order (e.g., Administer medication with food).

columns.name: orderReason
columns.description: Reason for the order (e.g., Patient experiencing pain).

columns.name: orderEntryMethodid
columns.description: Identifier for the method used to enter the order (e.g., 40, 41, 42).

columns.name: includeNow
columns.description: Indicates if the order should be included immediately (1) or not (0) (e.g., 0, 1).

columns.name: lastScheduleGenerateDate
columns.description: Date and time when the last schedule for the order was generated (e.g., 2021-08-01 14:45:00).

columns.name: discontinueReasonid
columns.description: Identifier for the reason the order was discontinued (e.g., 50, 51, 52).

columns.name: discontinuedDate
columns.description: Date and time when the order was discontinued (e.g., 2021-08-01 17:00:00).

columns.name: discontinuedBy
columns.description: Identifier for the user who discontinued the order (e.g., 60, 61, 62).

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: Indicates if the order has been deleted (1) or not (0) (e.g., 0, 1).

table_description: This table stores the acknowledgment information for each order, including the action type, who performed the action, and when the action was performed.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, and it is an auto-incrementing integer. It uniquely identifies each acknowledgment entry in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: orderid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `orders` table. It represents the order that the acknowledgment is associated with. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: actionType
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the type of action performed on the order. Example: 'approve', 'reject', 'cancel', etc.

columns.name: performedBy
columns.description: This is an integer column that stores the id of the user who performed the action. It can be a foreign key referring to the `id` column in the `users` table. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003, etc.

columns.name: performedDateTime
columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the action was performed. Example: '2021-09-01 12:34:56', '2021-09-02 14:23:12', etc.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that stores a boolean value (0 or 1) to indicate whether the acknowledgment entry has been deleted or not. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

table_description: This table stores the acknowledgment mapping information for orders.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: ackid
columns.description: The acknowledgment id associated with an order. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: ackBy
columns.description: The user id of the person who acknowledged the order. This can be a foreign key referring to the user's id in the `users` table (if exists). Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: ackFlag
columns.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the order has been acknowledged or not. '0' means not acknowledged, and '1' means acknowledged. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: ackDateTime
columns.description: The date and time when the order was acknowledged. Example: '2021-09-15 14:30:00', '2021-09-16 10:15:00'.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the record has been deleted or not. '0' means not deleted, and '1' means deleted. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores information about different programs associated with a particular patient.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which is an auto-incrementing integer value. It uniquely identifies each record in the table. Examples include 1, 2, 3, etc..

columns.name: Ptid
columns.description: This is a foreign key referring to the patient's id in another table (e.g., `patients` table). It is an integer value and represents the patient associated with the program. Examples include 101, 102, 103, etc..

columns.name: PtProgram
columns.description: This is an integer value representing the specific program associated with the patient. This is a foreign key referring to id column of referralpgms table.

columns.name: StartDt
columns.description: This is a varchar(25) column that stores the start date of the program in string format (e.g., '2021-01-01', '2021-02-15', '2021-03-20', etc.).

columns.name: EndDt
columns.description: This is a varchar(25) column that stores the end date of the program in a string format. Examples include '2021-12-31', '2021-11-30', '2021-10-15', etc..

columns.name: timestamp
columns.description: This is a timestamp column that stores the date and time when the record was last updated. It is automatically updated whenever the record is modified. Examples include '2021-01-01 12:34:56', '2021-02-15 10:20:30', '2021-03-20 18:45:22', etc..

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint(2) column that indicates whether the record has been deleted or not. A value of '0' means the record is active, while a value of '1' means the record has been deleted (0 = active and 1 = inactive).

table_description: This table stores Patient-Specific Alerts.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is an auto incremented Primary Key for This column .

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This column stores patient's id for whom alert is created. This column refers column UID from user table.

columns.name: Itemid
columns.description: This column stores itemid for the corresponding lab/DI/Procedure/Billing/Dental.This column refers column itemid from items table. If Other is selected int the user interfaceit inserts 0 as a value into this column.

columns.name: Name

columns.name: endDt
columns.description: This column stores the date till the alert is complaint. The format used is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

columns.name: frequency
columns.description: This column stores the frequency of the alert created.

columns.name: freqFlag
columns.description: This column stores one of the below values indicating the frequency unit. Y - Years, M - Months, W - Weeks and D - Days.

columns.name: alertType
columns.description:
This column stores one of the below values indicating type of the alert. Values: BillingAlert,
Immunizations,
Labs,
Other,
Procedures,
XRays.

columns.name: Providerid
columns.description: This column is not used anymore.

columns.name: ProviderName
columns.description: This column is not used anymore.

columns.name: IsRecurrent

table_description: This table stores customization settings for specific patients, including activation and duration of electronic messages.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key and an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: pid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `patients` table. It represents the unique identifier of the patient for whom the customization settings are being stored. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: activateEmsg
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether electronic messages are activated for the patient or not. A value of '1' means activated, and '0' means not activated. Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: eMsgFrom
columns.description: This is a date column that specifies the start date for sending electronic messages to the patient. Example: '2022-01-01', '2022-02-15'.

columns.name: eMsgTo
columns.description: This is a date column that specifies the end date for sending electronic messages to the patient. Example: '2022-12-31', '2022-03-31'.

columns.name: enableEMsg
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether electronic messages are enabled for the patient or not. A value of '1' means enabled, and '0' means not enabled. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores Ask at Order Entry (AOE) questions associated with a lab or diagnostic imaging order for a lab company.

columns.name: Qsid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each question with an integer value. For example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: OBRCode
columns.description: This column stores a lab code associated with the AOE question. This column refers to the column code from the labcodes table.

columns.name: OBXCode
columns.description: This column stores a question (observation or result) code associated with the AOE question added by the end user.

columns.name: Question
columns.description: The text of the question stored as a varchar(255). For example: What is your favorite color?, How old are you?.

columns.name: Questip
columns.description: Additional information or tips related to the question stored as a varchar(255). For example: Choose one color, Enter your age in years.

columns.name: ABN
columns.description: A flag indicating if the question is related to an abnormal result stored as a char(1). For example: Y for yes, N for no.

columns.name: labid
columns.description: This column stores the lab id of the company selected for the lab order associated with this AOE question.

columns.name: FieldType
columns.description: An enumeration representing the type of input field for the question, with possible values FT (Free Text), DD (Drop-down), ST (Single Text), RB (Radio Button), and CB (Check Box). For example: FT, DD.

columns.name: Required
columns.description: This column stores a value 0 or 1. 1 - when this question is marked as mandatory, 0- otherwise.

columns.name: itemid
columns.description: An integer identifier for the item associated with the question, with a default value of 0. For example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: MaxChar
columns.description: The maximum number of characters allowed for the answer stored as an int(2) with a default value of 0. For example: 50, 100.

columns.name: defaultvalue
columns.description: The default value for the answer stored as a varchar(255) with a default value of an empty string. For example: N/A, 18.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column stores a flag 0 or 1. 1 - when this AOE question is marked as deleted. 0 - otherwise.

columns.name: groupid
columns.description: This column stores the group id to which the answer options are associated to for this AOE question.

columns.name: inactive
columns.description: This column stores the flag value where 0 means active record and 1 means inactive record.

table_description: This table stores information about the answer to the question associated with Ask at Order Entry (AOE) with a lab or diagnostic imaging order.

columns.name: answer

columns.name: Answercode

columns.name: AnsweredBy

columns.name: AnsweredDate

columns.name: AnsweredTime

columns.name: labid

columns.name: id

columns.name: UID

columns.name: DocName

columns.name: value

columns.name: pagenum

columns.name: completed

columns.name: lastSubmittedQuestion

columns.name: uploadDateTime

columns.name: source

columns.name: ptSubmittimestamp

columns.name: msggUID
columns.description: Varchar (40) containing a message GUID can be NULL. Example: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000.

columns.name: questType

table_description: This table stores information about race codes, their names, CDC race values, and flags for favorites and user interface visibility.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which stores a unique integer identifier for each race code entry. It is an auto-incrementing value. For example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: Code
columns.description: This column stores a short string (up to 6 characters) representing the race code. For example: AA, HISP, ASIAN.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: This column stores the full name of the race code, with a maximum length of 100 characters. For example: African American, Hispanic, Asian.

columns.name: CDCRace
columns.description: This column stores the CDCRace value associated with the race code, with a maximum length of 100 characters. For example: Black or African American, "Hispanic or Latino, Asian.

columns.name: Favorite
columns.description: This is a tinyint(1) column that stores a boolean value (0 or 1) indicating whether the race code is marked as a favorite. For example: 0 (not a favorite), 1 (favorite).

columns.name: UIFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint(1) column that stores a boolean value (0 or 1) indicating whether the race code is visible in the user interface. For example: 0 (not visible), 1 (visible).

table_description: This table stores data related to patient's race.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the raceothers table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: pid

columns.name: name
columns.description: This column stores the name of the race of a patient. (i.e., Asian, White, etc.).

columns.name: code
columns.description: This column stores a code for a race.

table_description: this table store the process(scrubbed) encounter data

columns.name: id

columns.name: encid
columns.description: identifier for the encounter associated with the claim. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: jobid
columns.description: identifier for the job associated with the claim. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: eligibilityStatus
columns.description: Status of the claim's eligibility, represented as a string. Example: Eligible, Not Eligible.

columns.name: Claimid
columns.description: identifier for the claim associated with the encounter. Example: 5001, 5002, 5003.

columns.name: ValidationStatus
columns.description: A tinyint value representing the validation status of the claim. Example: 0 (Not Validated), 1 (Validated).

columns.name: jsValidation
columns.description: A tinyint value representing the JavaScript validation status of the claim. Example: 0 (Not Validated), 1 (Validated).

columns.name: created_datetime
columns.description: The date and time when the record was created. Example: 2021-09-01 12:34:56.

columns.name: deleteflag

columns.name: trUserid

table_description: This table stores information about reconciled data related to patients, including file details and reconciliation dates.

columns.name: ReconcileId
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and is an integer that uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is auto-incremented, so each new record will have a unique value. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: PatientId
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `Patient` table's primary key (`PatientId`). It is an integer that represents the unique identifier of the patient associated with the reconciled data. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: FileName
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the name of the file associated with the reconciled data. Example: "patient_data_101.csv", "patient_data_102.csv", etc.

columns.name: InterfaceName
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the name of the interface used for the reconciliation process. Example: "Interface1", "Interface2", etc.

columns.name: Description
columns.description: This is a text column that stores a detailed description of the reconciled data. Example: "Reconciled patient data from Hospital A and Hospital B."

columns.name: ReconciledDate
columns.description: This is a date column that stores the date when the data was reconciled. Example: "2021-08-01", "2021-08-02", etc.

columns.name: FilePath
columns.description: This is a varchar column that stores the file path where the reconciled data file is stored. Example: "/reconciled_data/patient_data_101.csv", "/reconciled_data/patient_data_102.csv", etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This is an integer column that indicates whether the record has been deleted or not. A value of 1 means the record is deleted, and a value of 0 means the record is not deleted. Example: 0, 1.

table_description: This table stores a list of documents attached to referrals.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is auto-incremented primary key in This column .

columns.name: Refid
columns.description: This column stores id of a referral to which documents are attached. This column refers to referralid column in referral stable.

columns.name: doctype
columns.description: This column stores id to indicate type of a document attached to referral. This column refers to id column in documentfolders table.

columns.name: docid
columns.description: This column stores id of a document attached to referral. This column refers to docid column in document table.

table_description: This table stores logs for past and rescheduled appointments based on patient referral.

columns.name: refid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a referral created by provider/staff  for which patient is visiting the referred provider. This column refers to referralid column in the referral table.

columns.name: logDate
columns.description: A date representing the date when the log was created. Example: 2021-09-15.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: An integer representing the unique user id associated with the appointment log. Example: 42.

columns.name: username
columns.description: A string (up to 255 characters) representing the username of the user associated with the appointment log. Example: johndoe.

columns.name: prevappt
columns.description: A string (up to 22 characters) representing the previous appointment date in a human-readable format. Example: 2021-08-25 14:30:00.

columns.name: reschdate
columns.description: A string (up to 22 characters) representing the rescheduled appointment date in a human-readable format. Example: 2021-09-10 10:00:00.

table_description: This table stores information about patient Incoming/Outgoing referrals, including details about the referral source, destination, dates, and status.

columns.name: Referralid
columns.description: Unique identifier for each referral record.

columns.name: patientid
columns.description: This column store the id of a patient for whom the referral has been created/received. This column refers to the UID in the user table.

columns.name: insid
columns.description: This column stores the id of an insurance being used for the referral. This column refers to insid column in the insurance table.

columns.name: refFrom
columns.description: This column stores the id of the provider selected under the From section in the user interface. Provider is someone who is referring the patient. This column refers to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: authNo
columns.description: This column refers to free text string entered into Auth Code filled in the user interface. This code represents Auth Code provided by the insurance company for the referral.

columns.name: date
columns.description: This column stores date on which the referral was created for the patient. Date is stored in YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.000 format.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: This column stores reason why the referral was created. Reason could be free text or pre-configured keywords selected by the provider/staff.

columns.name: diagnosis
columns.description: This column stores an id for a diagnosis for which the referral has been created. This column refers to the itemid column in the items table. Column has been declared as VARCHAR because this column may store multiple ids for diagnosis separated by '|' (i.e., 250909|252643).

columns.name: refStDate
columns.description: This column stores start date of the referral after which the referral can be used by the patient for the visit and the date is selected by provider/staff.

columns.name: refEnddate
columns.description: This column stores the end date of the referral after which referral can not be used by the patient and the date is selected by provider/staff.

columns.name: visitsAllowed
columns.description: This column stores a number, which represents number of visits to referred provider will be allowed with the referral.

columns.name: visitsUsed
columns.description: This column stores a number, which represents the number of visits to the referred provider patient has used with the referral.

columns.name: RefTo
columns.description: This column stores an id of a provider under the To section in the user interface. Provider is to whom the patient has been referred to.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: This column stores free text notes documented by provider/staff under General Notes section under the Notes tab in the user interface.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the referral has been deleted or not. 0 - Referral is not deleted, 1 - Referral is deleted.

columns.name: referralType
columns.description: This column stores a character I/O to indicate type of the referral being stored. I - Incoming Referral, O - Outgoing Referral.

columns.name: priority
columns.description: This column stores the priority of the referral documented by provider/staff. 0 - Routine, 1 - Urgent, 2 - Stat.

columns.name: assignedto
columns.description: This column stores name of the provider/staff to whom this referral has been assigned to in the user interface by the end user.

columns.name: assignedToid
columns.description: This column stores the id of a provider/staff to whom the referral has been assigned to in the user interface by the end user. This column refers to the UID column in the user table.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This column stores current status of the referral. Open - Referral is open, Pending - Consultation is Pending, Addressed - Referral is addressed, To Be Reconciled, Insurance Auth, Internal Review.

columns.name: authtype
columns.description: This column stores value of field Auth Type (Authorization Type) selected by the end user in the user interface.

columns.name: procedures
columns.description: This column stores an id for a procedure selected by provider/staff in the user interface while creating the referral. This column refers to the itemid column in the items table.

columns.name: fromfacility
columns.description: This column stores the id of a facility selected by the end user under the From section in the user interface while creating the referral. This column refers to the id column in the edi_facilities table.

columns.name: ToFacility
columns.description: This column stores the id of a facility selected by the end user under the To section in the user interface while creating the referral. This column refers to the id column in the edi_facilities table.

columns.name: speciality
columns.description: This column stores the id for a specialty of the practice for which the referral has been created. This column refers to the id column in the edi_speciality column.

columns.name: POS
columns.description: This column stores a code associated with the Place of Service. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) maintain POS codes used throughout the health care industry.

columns.name: UnitType
columns.description:
This column stores values from the Unit Type field in the user interface.
As per the practice, the unit type describes the nature of the visit for the referral created. The entity who receives the referral knows what kind of visit is required for that patient based on the unit type.

columns.name: FrontOfficeAuth
columns.description: This column stores flag 0/1 to indicate whether the referral record has been authorized by the front office staff to be uploaded to eHX or not. 0 - is not authorized, 1 -authorized by front office. This authorization is needed to send referral to eHX.

columns.name: ReferralNumber
columns.description: This column stores the Referral Number provided by a payer for prior authorization of a referral. If the Referral Number is missing and if the insurance 'requires referral,' then the claim can not be generated.

columns.name: apptDate
columns.description: This column stores the date for an appointment of a patient with referred provider.

columns.name: clinicalNotes
columns.description: This column stores free text notes documented by provider/staff under the Clinical Notes section under the Notes tab in the user interface.

columns.name: ReceivedDate
columns.description: This column stores date from the Received Date field in the user interface. Date when referral was received.

columns.name: refEncid
columns.description: identifier for the encounter associated with the referral.

columns.name: ApptTime
columns.description: This column stores the time for an appointment of a patient with referred provider associated with the referral.

columns.name: extNHXApptBlockid
columns.description: External appointment block identifier associated with the referral.

columns.name: extNHXRefTxid
columns.description: This column stores transaction id for the referral from P2P server. Transaction id is transmitted by P2P server outgoing when referral has been successfully received on the P2P server.

columns.name: refReqid
columns.description: identifier for the referral request. This column refers to the reqid column of the nhxreferral table.

columns.name: refFromP2pNPI
columns.description: National Provider identifier (NPI) of the referring provider.

columns.name: refFromName
columns.description: This column stores name of the referring provider.

columns.name: refToP2pNPI
columns.description: This column stores National Provider identifier (NPI) number of the referred provider. This column refers to NPI column in doctors table.

columns.name: refToName
columns.description: This column stores name of the referred provider.

columns.name: uploadedToPtDocs
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether documents received in incoming referral have been moved to the Patient Document section or not. 1 - If documents are moved to Patient Document, 0 - Otherwise.

columns.name: refToCCNameList
columns.description: This column stores comma separated names of providers added as CC while using the Send P2P Patient Record feature.

columns.name: refToCCNPIList
columns.description: This column stores comma separated National Provider identifiers (NPI) of providers added as CC while using the Send P2P Patient Record feature.

columns.name: p2pDeliveryStatus
columns.description: This column stores delivery status of the P2P referral if the referral has been sent electronically. 1 - Success, 2 - Failed, 3 - Partial Failed, 4 - In Transit.

columns.name: statusUpdateDate
columns.description: This column stores the time stamp when the p2pDeliveryStatus is updated.

columns.name: ccdaValidationStatus
columns.description: This column stores whether the CCDA attached to the electronic transaction satisfies MU eligibility criteria. 1 - CCDA failed MU eligibility criteria, 2 - CCDA passed MU eligibility criteria, 0 - Could not validate CCDA for MU eligibility.

columns.name: fromDirectAddress
columns.description: This column stores the direct registered health address of the provider who is sending outgoing referral out of the eClinicalWorks network.

columns.name: toDirectAddress
columns.description: This column stores the direct registered health address of the provider to whom the outgoing referral out of eClinicalWorks network is being sent to.

columns.name: toDirectAddress1
columns.description: Alternative direct address of the receiving provider.

columns.name: modifiedDate
columns.description: This column stores the time stamp if any modification is made on the referral by the end user.

columns.name: isVoiceMsgSent
columns.description: Flag indicating if a voice message has been sent for the referral (0 for not sent, 1 for sent).

columns.name: isTextMsgSent
columns.description: Flag indicating if a text message has been sent for the referral (0 for not sent, 1 for sent).

columns.name: quesAnsGUID
columns.description: When SmartReferralPractice is enabled, a practice can setup the questionnaire for out-of-network referrals. When a user tries to send out-of-network referrals, he/she has to fill out the questionnaire which then is saved on P2P. The GUID for the answers is generated on P2P and saved in this column.

columns.name: innetwork
columns.description: When SmartReferralPractice is enabled, this column stores values 0/1 to indicate if the provider to whom the referral is being sent to is in-network or not.  0 - if provider is out-of-network, 1 -  if provider is in-network.

columns.name: faxreferralxml
columns.description: When SmartReferralPractice is enabled, if the user tries to print/fax a referral, the XML for that referral is stored in this column. This XML is then synced to P2P for reporting.

columns.name: isHealowAppt
columns.description: This column stores 0/1 to indicate whether the referral appointment is from healow or not. 0 - Not a healow Appointment, 1 - healow Appointment.

columns.name: transportationRequired
columns.description: This column stores flags 0/1 to indicate whether the patient would require transportation during the referral visit or not. 0 - Transportation is not required, 1 -  Transportation is required. Custom column for Humana.

columns.name: approvalReq
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the referral is submitted for approval or not.  0 - Referral is not submitted for approval, 1 -  Referral is submitted for approval.

columns.name: approvalstatus
columns.description: This column stores values 0/1 to indicate whether the referral is approved or not. 0 - Referral is not approved, 1 - Referral is approved.

columns.name: EMCodes
columns.description: This column stores Evaluation and Management Codes (EM Codes) documented by end user under procedures section of the User Interface.

columns.name: subStatus
columns.description: This column stores status from the Sub Status field in the User Interface. This is an extension to the main status of a referral. Substatuses are user defined and comes from referralstatus table.

columns.name: subStatusid
columns.description: This column stores id of a Status from the Sub Status field in the User Interface. 0 - No Sub Status Selected, 1 - Not Completed

columns.name: isHISPTxCapable
columns.description: When sending electronic referral this column stores whether the receiver is a non-eCW HISP outbound receiver. 0 - Not non-eCW HISP outbound receiver, 1 - is non-eCW HISP outbound receiver. If value is 1, attachment size limitation can be adjusted accordingly.

columns.name: isReceiverFTPEnabled
columns.description: This column store values 0/1 to indicate of FTP is enabled for the provider to whom the referral is being sent to. 1-  If receiver's FTP is enabled, otherwise -0. If value is 1, attachment size limitation can be adjusted accordingly.

columns.name: totalAttSize
columns.description: This column stores total size of attachments to the referral in Kilo Bytes(KB).

columns.name: PMReferralid
columns.description: This column stores id for incoming referrals for which approval status was received over the referral interface. This column refers to Referralid column in pmreferrals table.(Check with Bhawna's Team)

columns.name: referralsubType
columns.description: Column stores sub type of a referral. Column stored values like "Visit", "CPT" etc

columns.name: cptunitsallowed
columns.description: Number of CPT (Current Procedural Terminology) units allowed for the referral.

columns.name: cptunitsused
columns.description: This column stores number of CPT units used for a referral.

columns.name: transmissionMethod
columns.description: Method of Transmision for Referral i.e., Print,Fax,P2P etc.

columns.name: isConsultNoteAttached
columns.description: Flag indicating if a consult note is attached to the referral (0 for not attached, 1 for attached).

columns.name: notify_portal
columns.description: Flag indicating if the referral should be notified on the patient portal (0 for not notified, 1 for notified).

columns.name: referral360id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the 360 referral.

table_description: This table stores the reasons for addendums in referrals, linking a referral to a specific reason for the addendum.

columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which is an auto-incrementing integer value. It uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: referralid

columns.name: reasonid
columns.description: This is a foreign key column that refers to the `structured_addendum_reason` table's `reasonid` column. It stores the id of the reason for the addendum in the referral. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

table_description: This table is used as a mapping table for referrals created for patients in a corrections facility.

columns.name: Id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the referral_correctional table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: ReferralId
columns.description: Unique identifier for each referral. This column is a foreign key that refers to the `Id` column in another table (e.g., `referrals` table). Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: BookAndCaseNo
columns.description: This column stores the BookAndCaseNo of the patient. Its has reference  to patients_correctional.BookAndCaseNo column.

columns.name: DeleteFlag
columns.description: This column stores the value 1 or 0. Its used to determine if record is deleted.

columns.name: Patients_Correctional_Id
columns.description: This column stores reference to column patients_correctional.Id

table_description: This table stores the reasons for noncompliance associated with each referral.

columns.description: This is the primary key column, which uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented when a new record is added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: referralId
columns.description: This column stores the referral ID associated with the noncompliance reason. It is an integer value and has a foreign key relation with the `referral` table's `ReferralId` column. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: reasonId
columns.description: This column stores the noncompliance reason ID associated with the referral. It is an integer value and has a foreign key relation with the `structured_noncompliance_reason` table's `reasonId` column. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

table_description: This table stores addendums related to referrals after they are marked as addressed., including the user who created the addendum and the date and time it was created.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is auto-incremented primary key in This column  which uniquely identify each record in This column .

columns.name: referralid
columns.description: This column stores id of a referral for which addendum is being added by the end user. This column refers to referralid column in referral table.

columns.name: userid
columns.description: This column stores id of a user who has added addendum to a referral. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: date
columns.description: This column stores date on which addendum was added to a referral by end user. Date is stored in "YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00.000" format.

columns.name: time
columns.description: This column stores time at which addendum was added to a referral by end user. Time is stored in "1900-01-01 hh:mm:ss.000" format.

columns.name: addendum
columns.description: This column stores text of an addendum added by end user to a referral.

table_description: This table stores the number of visits used by patients from the total allowed referral visits.

columns.name: referralid
columns.description: This column stores if od a referral created by provider/staff for which patient is visiting the referred provider. This column refers to referralid column in referral table.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores id of an encounter used during the visit for referral. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: visitNo
columns.description: This column stores number of visit patient is using to see referred provider.

columns.name: invoiceId
columns.description: This column is not in use currently.

columns.name: unitsUsed
columns.description: This column is not in use currently.

table_description: This table stores information about referral details for reporting purposes, including the sender and receiver's information, message type, and other related data.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: referralid
columns.description: Identifier for the referral, can be NULL. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: msgtype
columns.description: Message type as a tiny integer, can be NULL. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: from_npi
columns.description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the sender, can be NULL. Example: 1234567890, 2345678901.

columns.name: from_id
columns.description: Identifier for the sender, can be NULL. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003.

columns.name: from_firstname
columns.description: First name of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: 'John', 'Jane'.

columns.name: from_lastname
columns.description: Last name of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: 'Doe', 'Smith'.

columns.name: from_zipcode
columns.description: Zip code of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: '12345', '67890'.

columns.name: from_taxonomycode
columns.description: Taxonomy code of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: '207Q00000X', '207R00000X'.

columns.name: from_specialty
columns.description: Specialty of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: 'Family Medicine', 'Internal Medicine'.

columns.name: from_apuid
columns.description: Identifier for the sender's APU (Accountable Provider Unit), can be NULL. Example: 2001, 2002, 2003.

columns.name: from_practicename
columns.description: Practice name of the sender, default is an empty string. Example: 'ABC Clinic', 'XYZ Hospital'.

columns.name: to_npi
columns.description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the receiver, can be NULL. Example: 3456789012, 4567890123.

columns.name: to_id
columns.description: Identifier for the receiver, can be NULL. Example: 3001, 3002, 3003.

columns.name: to_firstname
columns.description: First name of the receiver, default is an empty string. Example: 'Alice', 'Bob'.

columns.name: to_lastname
columns.description: Last name of the receiver, default is an empty string. Example: 'Johnson', 'Brown'.

columns.name: to_zipcode
columns.description: Zip code of the receiver, default is an empty string. Example: '98765', '43210'.

columns.name: to_taxonomycode
columns.description: Taxonomy code of the receiver, default is an empty string. Example: '208M00000X', '208D00000X'.

columns.name: to_specialty
columns.description: Specialty of the receiver, default is an empty string. Example: 'Pediatrics', 'Dermatology'.

table_description: This table stores the results of report writers, including notes, report and template IDs, document IDs, and whether the report is editable or not.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key, an integer that uniquely identifies each report writer result. Example: 1, 2, 3.

columns.name: notes
columns.description:
This column is used to store the final result of report writer. 
As per requirement, user can add up to 80,000 characters. Hence, added this column as Text/Varchar(Max).  As per requirement, user can not enter NULL value from UI. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here.

columns.name: reportid
columns.description: This column is used to store reportid of associated DI. Report writer result can associate with other entity apart from reportid. Hence, added this column as NULL. This column is a foreign key that references to labdata (reportid). Reportid column of labdata is INT type. Hence, INT datatype is suitable here.

columns.name: templateid
columns.description:
This column is used to store template id of associated template. 
Report writer result should be associated with specific template. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here. This column is a foreign key that references to report_writer_template (templateid). Templateid column of report_writer_template is INT type. Hence, INT datatype is suitable here.

columns.name: docid
columns.description: This column is used to store generated Document id once user click on Publish Report button to generated PDF. By default, value of this column will be NULL. When user click Publish Report, the system will generate document and add associated docid in this column. Hence, added this column as NULL. This column is a foreign key that references to document (docid), docid column of document is INT type. Hence, INT datatype is suitable here.

columns.name: isReportEditable
columns.description:
This column is used to maintain flag to update Report Writer details.
0: Report Writer details not editable
1: Report Writer details editable
The default value of this column is 1, so Report Writer tab will be editable. Once the user clicks Publish Report button and the PDF is generated, this column is 0 which will make the Report Writer details disabled. Once the user clicks Edit Report, this will change to 1. This column can have only 0 or 1 value. Hence, TINYINT is suitable for this column.

table_description: This table stores information about sentences used in report writing, including their order, relationships to other sentences, and whether they are triggered or child sentences.

columns.name: sentenceid
columns.description: This is the primary key and an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each sentence in the table.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: This column is used to store the sentence.�As per requirement, user can not enter NULL value. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here. As per requirements, user can add up to 40,000 characters for each sentence. Hence, Text/varchar*max) column type is suitable here.

columns.name: sectionid
columns.description: This column is used to store id of section table.�Each sentence should associated with particular section. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here. This column is a foreign key that references to report_writer_section (sectionid). Sectionid column of report_writer_section is INT type. Hence, INT datatype is suitable here.

columns.name: sentenceOrder
columns.description: This column is used to store sequence number of sentence.�Each sentence should have associated order index. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here. Each section can have multiple sentences and usesr can change order of each sentence. Hence, this column has INT datatype.

columns.name: isTriggeredSentence
columns.description: This column is used to store triggered sentence details.�As per requirement by default sentence should not be triggered sentence. Hence, default value of this column is 0. Each sentence should have 0 or 1 value. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here. 0: Sentence is not a triggered sentence. 1: Sentence is triggered sentence. This column can have only 0 or 1 value. Hence, TINYINT is suitable for this column.

columns.name: isChildSentence
columns.description:
This column is used to store details about child sentence. As per requirement, by default, sentence should not be child sentence. Hence, default value of this column is 0. Each sentence should have 0 or 1 value. Hence, not NULL constraint is suitable here.

0: Sentence is not a child sentence�
1: Sentence is child sentence

This column can have only 0 or 1 value. Hence, TINYINT is suitable for this column.

columns.name: parentSentenceid
columns.description:
This column is used to store parent sentence id if this sentence is child sentence. The default value of this column is NULL. If a child sentence has a column value as 1, then only this column will have a parent sentence id. 
This column will have sentenceid. Hence, INT datatype is suitable here.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description:
This column is used for soft deleting records, the value should be 1 or 0.
By default all sentence should not be deleted. Hence, default value of this column is 0. 
1 : Deleted
0 : Not Deleted
This column can have only 0 or 1 value. Hence, TINYINT is suitable for this column.

1 : Deleted�
