table_description: This table stores information about different vision test types performed during an encounter.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table and is an auto-incrementing integer value. It uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: ENCOUNTERid
columns.description: This column contains the encounterid value. It refers to enc table `encounterid` column. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: VISIONRXid
columns.description: identifier for the specific vision test performed. This is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `visionrx` table. Example: 1001, 1002, 1003, etc.

columns.name: ITEMid
columns.description: identifier for the specific item related to the vision test type. It refers to items table `itemid` column. Example: 5001, 5002, 5003, etc.

columns.name: ITEM_NAME
columns.description: Name of the specific item related to the vision test type. It refers to items table `itemName` column. Example: 'Visual Acuity', 'Color Vision', 'Depth Perception'.

table_description: This table stores the log information related to updates in the VisionRx system for patients and their encounters.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key of the table, which is an integer value that uniquely identifies each record in the table. It is auto-incremented, meaning that the value increases automatically for each new record added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encounterId
columns.description: This is a foreign key column that refers to the `id` column in the `encounters` table. It is an integer value that represents the unique identifier of the encounter associated with the vision prescription. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: formattedString
columns.description: This is a varchar(80) column that stores a formatted string representation of the vision prescription. It has a maximum length of 80 characters and cannot be NULL. Example: "OD: -1.00, OS: -1.25, PD: 62"

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint(2) column that indicates whether the record has been deleted or not. It has a default value of '0', which means the record is not deleted. If the value is '1', the record is considered deleted. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted)

table_description: This table stores the logs of copying visits between players and their injuries.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, which uniquely identifies each record. It is an integer value that is automatically incremented as new records are added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encounterId
columns.description: This column stores the integer value of the encounter ID associated with the vision prescription. It is a foreign key that refers to the `id` column in the `encounters` table. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: deleteFlag
columns.description: This is a tinyint column that indicates whether the record has been marked for deletion or not. It has a default value of '0', which means the record is not marked for deletion. A value of '1' indicates that the record is marked for deletion. Example: 0 (not marked for deletion), 1 (marked for deletion).

table_description: This table stores information about vision and vergence tests performed during an eye examination.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key for the table, an automatically incremented integer that uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This is a foreign key that refers to the `encounterid` column in the `enc` table. It represents the id of the encounter during which the vision and vergence tests were performed. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.name: examtype
columns.description: This is a tiny integer column that stores the type of eye examination performed. Example: 0, 1, 2, etc.

columns.name: dist_blur
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the distance at which the patient's vision starts to blur during the test. Example: 50, 100, 150, etc.

columns.name: dist_break
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the distance at which the patient's vision breaks during the test. Example: 60, 120, 180, etc.

columns.name: dist_recovery
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the distance at which the patient's vision recovers during the test. Example: 70, 140, 210, etc.

columns.name: near_blur
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the near distance at which the patient's vision starts to blur during the test. Example: 10, 20, 30, etc.

columns.name: near_break
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the near distance at which the patient's vision breaks during the test. Example: 15, 25, 35, etc.

columns.name: near_recovery
columns.description: This is a small integer column that stores the near distance at which the patient's vision recovers during the test. Example: 20, 30, 40, etc.

table_description: This table stores information about the visit type codes, which define the type of the patients' visits.

columns.name: CodeId
columns.description: The column stores an id of the Visit Type Code. This is an auto incremented primary key of This column .

columns.name: Name
columns.description: This column stores a Name of visit type code.

columns.name: Description
columns.description: This column stores description of the visit type code.

columns.name: ChartTitle
columns.description: This column stores chart title of the visit type code.

columns.name: color
columns.description: This column stores a color for the visit type. This color is the outline color for the appointment.

columns.name: phyFlag
columns.description: Flag related to the physician (e.g., 'Y', 'N').

columns.name: visitType
columns.description: This column stores visit type from the Pre-defined options to determine the format and content of the Progress Notes to be used for the corresponding appointment.

columns.name: obGyn
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to include the OB/GYN History section in the Progress Notes for this visit type.  0 - Not Include , 1 - Include

columns.name: PhysicalTherapy
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to include the Physical Therapy Assessment section in the Progress Notes for this visit type.  0 - Not Include , 1 - Include

columns.name: ReqClaim
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate the visit is billable. 0 - Not Billable , 1 - Billable.

columns.name: ReqCopay
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate the co-payments is required for the appointment with this Visit Type. 0 - Not Required , 1 - Required.

columns.name: pregVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a pregnancy visit. 0 - Non pregnancy visit, 1 - Pregnancy visit.

columns.name: Active
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate whether the visit type code is active or inactive. 0 - Inactive, 1 - Active.

columns.name: ProgDisplay
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate whether to display Appointments with this visit type in 'Progress Notes' visits Drop Down. 0 - Do not display, 1 - Display.

columns.name: OrthoVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a orthopedic visit. 0 - Non orthopedic visit, 1 - Orthopedic visit.

columns.name: VisionVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to include the Vision Examination section in the Progress Notes for encounters using this visit type. 0 - Not Include , 1 - Include.

columns.name: webVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 indicating   synchronize this visit type with the Patient Portal. 0 - Not synchronize , 1 - Synchronize.

columns.name: DentalVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a dental visit. 0 - Non dental visit, 1 - Dental visit.

columns.name: CarePlanVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to include appointments with this visit type in a care plan.  0 - Not Include , 1 - Include.

columns.name: segVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a patient housing. 0 - Non patient housing visit, 1 - Patient housing visit.

columns.name: vmsgspanishtext
columns.description: Column stores voice message in Spanish to be played for the visit type.

columns.name: txtspanishtext
columns.description: Column stores message in Spanish to be sent via text for the visit type.

columns.name: vmsgtemplatetext
columns.description: Column stores voice message in English to be played for the visit type.

columns.name: txttemplatetext
columns.description: Column stores message in English to be sent via text for the visit type.

columns.name: MUExclude
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to exclude any encounters using this visit type from Meaningful Use reporting. 0 - Not Exclude, 1 - Exclude.

columns.name: apptMachineEnglish
columns.description: Stores Appointment machine template(English) set by end user.

columns.name: apptMachineSpanish
columns.description: Stores Appointment machine template in Spanish which is set by end user.

columns.name: exclude
columns.description: Flag indicating if the visit is excluded (e.g., 0 for No, 1 for Yes).

columns.name: NuclearTestVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to enable worksheets that help specialists when documenting a patient visit. 0 - Disable, 1 - Enable.

columns.name: CareMgmtVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to to enable a Care Management visit for this visit type. 0 - Disable, 1 - Enable.

columns.name: AllowCurRxReconcilationVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to prevent medication reconciliation from taking place for encounters using this visit type. 0 - Not reconcile, 1 - Reconcile.

columns.name: CCMRVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a CCMR visit. 0 - Non CCMR visit, 1 - CCMR visit.

columns.name: nsexclude
columns.description: Stores values 0/1 to indicate whether to exclude this visit code from No Show reminders.

columns.name: ReferralVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate whether require referrals for encounters using this visit type. 0 - Not Required, 1 - Required.

columns.name: PhysicalTherapyVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a Physical Therapy visit. 0 - Non Physical Therapy visit, 1 - Physical Therapy visit.

columns.name: telemedVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a Helow Tele visit. 0 - Non Helow Tele visit, 1 - Helow Tele visit.

columns.name: DermVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to mark any appointment with this visit type as a dermatology visit. 0 - Non dermatology, 1 - Dermatology.

columns.name: allergyskintestvisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a allergy visit. 0 - Non allergy visit, 1 - Allergy visit.

columns.name: occHealthVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate any appointment with this Visit Type as a occ-health. 0 - Non occ-health visit, 1 - occ-health visit.

columns.name: enablecollectubclaimdata
columns.description: Stores values 0/1 to indicate whether to enable collectible claim data.  0 - Do not enable collectible claim data, 1 - Enable collectible claim data

columns.name: TCMVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate if the visit code is for Transition Care Management. 0 - Not a TCM visit code , 1 - TCM visit code.

columns.name: insplantype
columns.description: This column stores insurance plan type code from the pre-defined list of values. 0 - Medical , 1- Dental, 4 - Vision, 5 - Behavioral Health.

columns.name: ccmrGroupMaxCapacity
columns.description: Column stored default max capacity for Group encounters

columns.name: VascularVisit
columns.description: This column stores value 0/1 to indicate if the visit code is for Vascular module. 0 - Not a Vascular visit, 1 - visit code is for Vascular visit.

columns.name: rpmVisit
columns.description: Flag indicating if the visit is related to RPM (e.g., 0 for No, 1 for Yes).

columns.name: wellChildVisit
columns.description: Flag indicating if the visit is a well-child visit (e.g., 0 for No, 1 for Yes).

columns.name: rheumatologyVisit
columns.description: Flag indicating if the visit is related to rheumatology (e.g., 0 for No, 1 for Yes).

columns.name: warfarinFlowsheetVisit
columns.description: Flag indicating if the visit is related to warfarin flowsheet (e.g., 0 for No, 1 for Yes).

table_description: This table stores information about the visit status codes, which define the status of the patients' visits.

columns.name: code

columns.name: status

columns.name: color

table_description: This table stores the list of vital exceptions, including their reasons, display order, and deletion status.

columns.name: Id
columns.description: This is the primary key column, which stores a unique integer value for each record in the table. It is an auto-incrementing column, meaning that the value will automatically increase for each new record added. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: This column stores the reason for the exception as a string with a maximum length of 64 characters. Example: "System maintenance", "Data error", etc.

columns.name: displayIndex
columns.description: This column stores the display order of the exception as an unsigned tiny integer value. It is used to determine the order in which the exceptions should be displayed. Example: 0, 1, 2, etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This column stores the deletion status of the exception as an unsigned tiny integer value. A value of 0 indicates that the exception is active, while a value of 1 indicates that the exception has been deleted. Example: 0 (active), 1 (deleted).

table_description: This table stores the vitals recorded during patient encounters.

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: This column stores enocunterid for which vitals are being recorded. This column refers to encounterid column in enc table.

columns.name: vitalid
columns.description: This column stores itemid associated with name of the vitals being documented during the encounter. This column refers to itemid column in items table. Mapping of vital names and itemids are stored in vitaltypes table.

columns.name: propid
columns.description: This columns stores itemid to get unit of measurement (UOM). This column refers to itemid column in items table. Mapping of itemid and propid is stored in itemdetail table.

columns.name: value
columns.description: This column stores values for different vitals provided by end users during the encounter.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This column is auto-incremented primary key in This column .

columns.name: UpdatedBy
columns.description: This column stores user id of the provider/staff who updated/added vitals information for the encounter. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: UpdatedTime
columns.description: This column stores date and time when provider/staff added/updated vitals information. Column does not store individual time stamp for each vital for an encounter, time stamp is updated for all vitals even if one of the values is changed. time stamp is stored in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.sss' format.

columns.name: defaultValue
columns.description: A varchar(1024) field storing the default value for the vital property. Example: "97.0"

columns.name: valueHtm
columns.description: A text field that may store an HTML representation of the vital property value. Example: "98.6"

columns.name: value2
columns.description: This column stores value being documented by end user for  'vision' vital otherwise this column is left blank for other vitals.

columns.name: nottaken
columns.description: A tinyint(1) field indicating whether the vital was not taken (1) or taken (0). Example: 0

columns.name: exceptionid
columns.description: An integer representing the unique identifier for an exception related to the vital, if any. This column has a foreign key relation with the `vital_exceptionlist` table's `id` column. Example: 3

table_description: This table stores the history of vital sign measurements for patients during their encounters.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is auto-incremented primary key in This column .

columns.name: encounterid
columns.description: identifier for the encounter during which the vital sign was measured. This is a foreign key that refers to the `enc` table and its `encounterid` column. Example: 101, 102, 103.

columns.name: vitalid
columns.description: This column stores itemid associated with name of the vitals being documented during the encounter. This column refers to itemid column in items table. Mapping of vital names and itemids are stored in vitaltypes table.

columns.name: propid
columns.description: This columns stores itemid to get unit of measurement (UOM). This column refers to itemid column in items table. Mapping of itemid and propid is stored in itemdetail table.

columns.name: Value
columns.description: This column stores values with/without HTML tags for different vitals provided by end users during the encounter.

columns.name: UpdatedBy
columns.description: This column stores user id of the provider/staff who updated/added vitals information for the encounter. This column refers to UID column in user table.

columns.name: UpdatedTime
columns.description: This column stores time stamp when each individual vital was added and updated by provider/staff for an encounter. time stamp is stored in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.sss' format.

columns.name: displayorder
columns.description: This column stores order in which vitals are shown in the user interface.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This columns stores 0/1 values to indicate whether the vital was deleted or not. 0 - Not Deleted vital 1- Deleted Vital.

columns.name: value2
columns.description: This column stores values for different vitals provided by end users during the encounter. This column does not store HTML tags with values in this column.

columns.name: nottaken
columns.description: Tiny integer value to indicate if the vital sign was not taken (1) or taken (0). Example: 0, 1.

columns.name: exceptionid
columns.description: identifier for any exception related to the vital sign measurement. This is a foreign key that refers to the `vital_exceptionlist` table and its `id` column. Example: 1 (patient refused), 2 (equipment malfunction).

columns.name: updatedTimeinUTC
columns.description: time stamp in UTC of when the record was last updated. Example: "2021-09-01 08:34:56".

table_description: This table stores a log of vital sign measurements taken during patient encounters, including the values, actions taken, and exceptions.

columns.name: id

table_description: This table stores logs of actions performed on a waitlist, such as adding or removing items, along with details about the user, product, and changes made.

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is the primary key and an auto-incrementing integer that uniquely identifies each log entry in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.description: This is a datetime column that stores the date and time when the action was performed. Example: '2021-09-15 14:30:00'.

columns.name: uname
columns.description: This is a varchar(190) column that stores the username of the user who performed the action. Example: 'john_doe'.

columns.name: pid
columns.description: This is an int(11) column that stores the product ID associated with the action. This could be a foreign key referring to the product's ID in another table, such as a `products` table. Example: 101, 102, 103, etc.

columns.description: This is a varchar(190) column that stores the name of the product associated with the action. Example: 'Product A', 'Product B', 'Product C', etc.

columns.description: This is a varchar(50) column that stores the type of action performed on the waitlist, such as 'add', 'remove', or 'update'.

columns.name: modifiedfield
columns.description: This is a varchar(50) column that stores the name of the field that was modified during the action, if applicable. Example: 'quantity', 'price', 'status', etc.

columns.name: finalvalue
columns.description: This is a text column that stores the final value of the modified field after the action was performed. Example: '10', '25.99', 'In Stock', etc.

table_description: This table stores information about County information based on zip numbers

columns.name: id
columns.description: This is an auto-incrementing integer column that serves as the primary key for the table. It uniquely identifies each record in the table. Example: 1, 2, 3, etc.

columns.name: zipcode
columns.description: This is a varchar(10) column that stores the zip code. It is a required field and cannot be NULL. Example: "12345", "98765", "54321", etc.

columns.name: statecode
columns.description: This is a char(2) column that stores the state code. It is a required field and cannot be NULL. Example: "NY", "CA", "TX", etc.

columns.name: county
columns.description: This is a char(3) column that stores the county code. It is a required field and cannot be NULL. Example: "001", "002", "003", etc.

columns.name: deleteflag
columns.description: This is an int(2) column that stores a flag indicating whether the record is deleted or not. It has a default value of '0'. Example: 0 (not deleted), 1 (deleted).

columns.name: totaladdressratio
columns.description: This is a double column that stores the total address ratio for the given zip code, state code, and county code combination. It can be NULL if the ratio is not available. Example: 0.75, 1.0, 0.5, etc.
